title: Immutable LLM Run Configuration (spec 6.2)
status: FROZEN as amended 2026-09-18. No field in this document may be altered after the first scored LLM generation of run 2026-09-17-7677581. A change after that point requires a new benchmark run id. The 2026-09-18 amendments were made before any scored generation and before any score was computed, and are itemised in remediation_changelog.
fixed_column_order_note: This order is the fixed column order of every LLM Practical Effectiveness table. It is presentation order only and carries no weight.

fairness_declaration.purpose_statement: The benchmark's purpose is not to make Quidra score well. Quidra is the language under evaluation; the other nine are the fixed comparison set. Every language may score well on something Quidra does badly and badly on something Quidra does well.
fairness_declaration.nothing_derived_from_quidra: No task, oracle, prompt, metric definition, tolerance, tool permission, or weight in this document was derived from Quidra's syntax, operators, types, standard library, or feature set, WITH ONE DISCLOSED EXCEPTION: the frozen Park-Miller data generator was selected under the constraint recorded in methodology/00_cross_language_constraints.md C-1, whose selection criterion includes Quidra's overflow-checked integers among the ten languages the generator had to be exactly and idiomatically expressible in. C-1 records the neutrality argument and the verification that the generator requires no workaround and grants no shortcut in any of the ten. Every task is otherwise specified by required observable behaviour only.
fairness_declaration.no_capability_removed: No capability, boundary case, or error case was removed from the task set because Quidra lacks it or handles it awkwardly. Cases that Quidra's overflow-checked integers, its error model, or its interpreter path make harder for Quidra remain in the set. Conversely, no facility is left available to one language that the other nine must hand-build: see prohibited_facilities on PE-P5/PE-P6, which removes a Quidra advantage on the workload whose purpose is to measure building that facility.
fairness_declaration.identical_application: The system prompt, repair prompt, tool permissions, timeouts, retry policy, pack budget, examples budget, trial counts, oracles, and normalisation are byte-identical across all ten languages except for the enumerated placeholder substitutions in 'per_language_placeholder_substitutions', which carry only benchmark-controlled language-specific material (display name, toolchain version string, file extension, entry-point filename, and the frozen build/run recipe already recorded in environment.json).
fairness_declaration.no_fabrication: Where a quantity cannot be measured honestly with this client and toolchain, it is recorded as N/A with an explicit machine-readable reason in 'na_policy_for_llm_practical'. No value is estimated, inferred, or filled in from expectation.

model_and_client_identity.client: Claude Code agent harness (Claude Agent SDK)
model_and_client_identity.client_version_capture_rule: Spec 6.2 asks for 'API or client version'; the disjunction is satisfiable even though the provider API version string is not. The orchestrator captures the Claude Code CLI / Claude Agent SDK version string the harness reports (the CLI's own --version output and the SDK package version), once before the first scored trial, writes it into this field, and repeats it per trial in manifest.json under 'client_version_reported'. A trial whose reported client version differs from the frozen value is recorded in _deviations.json with class 'client_version_mismatch' and the run is not mixed across client versions. This field must be filled before the first scored trial; it is not left null.
model_and_client_identity.execution_mechanism: Each trial is executed by a freshly spawned subagent of the Claude Code agent harness, launched through the harness's Workflow tool by the benchmark orchestrator.
model_and_client_identity.api_version_reason: This client does not expose a PROVIDER API version string to the caller. Recorded as null rather than guessed. The client-side half of spec 6.2's 'API or client version' requirement is satisfied by 'client_version' above, which is captured, not guessed.
model_and_client_identity.model_change_policy: A model or version change requires a new benchmark run id and must not be mixed into run 2026-09-17-7677581. If the harness reports a different model identifier for any trial, that trial is invalidated, recorded in the deviation register, and re-run; if the identifier cannot be restored, the run is abandoned rather than mixed.
model_and_client_identity.model_identifier_recorded_per_trial: manifest.json of every trial records the model identifier AND the client version the harness reported for that trial. Trials whose recorded identifier is not exactly 'claude-opus-5' are excluded from scoring and listed in _deviations.json.

context_isolation.mechanism: Every initial trial is a newly spawned subagent with an empty context window. It receives only the system prompt, the task prompt, and the on-disk reference pack in its own trial working directory. It has no transcript, memory, summary, or artefact from any other trial, any other language, or the orchestrator's own conversation.
cross_trial_memory_enforcement: The subagent is spawned with no conversation history.
Each trial receives a private working directory; it cannot read another trial's directory because every path it is given is inside its own directory and the pack directory.
The trial working directory is created empty immediately before the trial and contains no output of any previous trial.
No orchestrator text summarising a previous trial appears in any trial prompt. The prompt templates in this document are the complete set of orchestrator-authored text a trial ever sees.
Repair turns continue inside the SAME subagent context as their initial generation (this is required: the model must see the program it wrote). Repair turns never cross trial boundaries.
context_isolation.satisfies_spec_6_2: This satisfies spec 6.2's requirements 'context: a fresh isolated conversation/session for every initial trial' and 'cross-trial memory: prohibited'.

decoding_controls._policy: Spec 6.2: if a provider or client does not expose one of temperature, top-p, seed, or token-limit controls, do not emulate it with a language-specific workaround; record the field as provider-controlled / unavailable, preserve provider defaults if known, and use the same interface and configuration for every language.

temperature.reason: The Claude Code agent harness does not expose a temperature parameter to a spawned subagent. No workaround is used.

top_p.reason: The Claude Code agent harness does not expose a top-p parameter to a spawned subagent. No workaround is used.

seed.reason: The Claude Code agent harness does not expose a decoding seed to a spawned subagent. No workaround is used, and no prompt noise is added to force or suppress diversity.

max_output_tokens_per_generation.reason: The harness does not expose a per-generation output-token limit to the caller. It is not emulated by instructing the model to be brief, because that would change generation behaviour and would not be a decoding control.

max_cumulative_output_tokens_per_trial.status: not enforceable as a hard limit
max_cumulative_output_tokens_per_trial.reason: The harness provides no cumulative output-token cap for a subagent. The budget is therefore not enforced.
max_cumulative_output_tokens_per_trial.accounting_actually_used: Cumulative token usage per trial is ACCOUNTED rather than capped. For each trial the orchestrator records, in tokens/usage.json, the harness-reported input tokens, output tokens, cache-read tokens and cache-creation tokens for the initial generation and for each repair turn separately, plus their per-trial sums. The trial is bounded instead by the wall-clock timeout and the fixed 3-repair budget, both of which are identical for all ten languages. If a trial's cumulative reported output tokens exceed 65,536 the trial is NOT truncated or discarded; the excess is recorded in manifest.json as budget_advisory_exceeded=true and published, so that the deviation from the spec default is visible rather than absorbed.

decoding_controls.duplication_reporting: If repeated trials in a cell produce byte-identical source, all trials are preserved and the duplication rate (identical-source trials / trials in cell) is published per language in raw/duplication_rate.json. No ad-hoc prompt noise is added to force diversity.
decoding_controls.identical_interface_across_languages: The same client, the same spawn mechanism, the same prompt templates, and the same (unavailable) decoding controls are used for every one of the ten languages. No language is generated through a different interface or configuration.

context_window_limit.reason: The per-subagent context window of the Claude Code agent harness is not configurable by the benchmark and is not reported to the caller as a number. It is identical for all ten languages because the same client and spawn mechanism is used for all of them.
context_window_limit.observable_handling: If a trial terminates because it exhausted its context, the harness surfaces this as a subagent termination. That outcome is then SPLIT by the mechanical stall test in retry_policy_infrastructure.agent_self_exhaustion_split, exactly as an agent wall-clock timeout is. A provider or transport stall is an INFRASTRUCTURE event of class 'context_exhausted_stalled' and is retried. A subagent that was actively generating or tool-calling until its context filled is NOT an infrastructure event: it is a model/language outcome, is classified from whatever exists at <trial>/generated/ by the ordinary ladder, is SCORED, and is recorded with subclass 'agent_budget_exhausted'. It is never recorded as a provider fault merely because the subagent stopped.
context_window_limit.mitigation: Diagnostic feedback in repair prompts is truncated to the frozen byte budget in 'repair_feedback_truncation' so that repair turns cannot grow without bound, identically for all languages.

repair_policy.who_performs_the_repair: The model, inside the same subagent context as its initial generation. The orchestrator supplies only real diagnostics and never proposes a fix, names a cause, points at a line, or hints at the language feature to use.
repair_policy.repair_trigger: A repair turn is issued if and only if the current version's classification is not PASS, and fewer than 3 repair turns have been used.
repair_policy.repair_stops_early: If a version classifies as PASS, no further repair turn is issued and the remaining repair budget is unused (recorded as repair_turns_used).

repair_feedback_truncation.rule: Each of BUILD_STDOUT, BUILD_STDERR, RUN_STDOUT, RUN_STDERR is included verbatim from its first byte up to 8000 bytes. If the stream is longer, the included text is followed by the literal line '[...truncated, N more bytes...]' with N the exact number of omitted bytes.
repair_feedback_truncation.oracle_diff_budget: At most the first 20 failing checks, each rendered as three lines: 'check <id>', 'expected: <expected>', 'actual: <actual>'. If more than 20 checks failed, followed by the literal line '[...N more failing checks...]'.
repair_feedback_truncation.rationale: Head truncation at a fixed byte budget is applied identically to every language. It is not tuned to any language's diagnostic verbosity, and the untruncated streams are preserved on disk for audit.

human_edit_prohibition.rule: PROHIBITED. Human edits to generated source counted as LLM success are prohibited (spec 9, spec 32).
enforcement_mechanism: M1. Write isolation. Only the trial subagent writes to <trial>/generated/. The orchestrator and every scoring script open that directory read-only. The scoring pipeline has no code path that writes a source file under trials/.

M2. Content hashing at the moment of capture. Immediately after the subagent returns, before any build or oracle step, the orchestrator computes SHA-256 of every file under <trial>/generated/ and writes it to <trial>/versions/<version>/sha256sums.txt, together with the file size and the filesystem mtime in nanoseconds.

M3. Re-verification at scoring. The scoring pass recomputes SHA-256 of every preserved source file and compares it to the recorded value. Any mismatch invalidates the trial, which is then recorded in _deviations.json with class 'source_mutated_after_capture' and excluded from all metrics. It is never silently repaired or re-run in place.
M4. Immutable copy. The captured source is additionally copied to <trial>/versions/<version>/source/ and to <trial>/final/source/ and those copies are chmod 0444 after writing.

M5. Tool-call audit. <trial>/logs/agent_tool_calls.jsonl records every tool call the subagent made, with timestamps. A third party can confirm that every mutation of generated/ was made by the subagent and by nothing else.

M6. Declaration. results/llm_practical_summary.md must carry the statement that no generated source was edited by a human, together with the count of trials whose hashes verified (which must equal the count of scored trials).
human_edit_prohibition.what_is_not_a_human_edit: The orchestrator creates the empty trial directory, creates the empty subdirectories <trial>/generated/, <trial>/scratch/ and <trial>/build/, writes the pack, writes prompts, and runs the frozen build/run commands. It empties <trial>/build/ immediately before each scored build and before each timed build in Generated Code Compile Performance, and recreates it empty. None of these touch or produce generated source. Creating the build output directory is a harness convention that the harness satisfies (spec 10.4 pre-flight item (b)): the frozen build commands of C++, Rust, Swift, Zig, Quidra and Go write into build/ and fail with 'no such file or directory' when it is absent, while javac -d and tsc --outDir create it themselves; leaving it to the model would manufacture a COMPILE_FAIL for six languages and not for the other four. The orchestrator never fixes a filename, a file extension, an entry-point name, or a stray character in generated source; if the model wrote the file to the wrong path or with the wrong name, that is a generation failure and is scored as one.

external_retrieval_prohibition.rule: PROHIBITED during primary generation and during every repair turn, except for benchmark-supplied specifications, references, source code, tests, and compiler/runtime diagnostics (spec 6.2).
what_is_permitted: The task specification text in the trial prompt.
Every file under <trial>/pack/ (language reference pack, worked examples, build/run recipe, and for Scenario B the benchmark-supplied reference source).
Any file the subagent itself wrote under <trial>/generated/ or <trial>/scratch/.
Real stdout/stderr and exit codes from building, running, or testing the subagent's own program with the frozen toolchain.

Locally installed compiler/runtime help output invoked by the subagent (for example a --help or --version flag on the frozen toolchain), because that is part of the toolchain and is available identically to all ten languages.
external_retrieval_prohibition.enforcement_in_the_trial_prompt: Rule 3 of the system prompt states the prohibition explicitly, names the only permitted reference locations, and states that attempting network retrieval invalidates the trial. The same sentence is given to all ten languages.
external_retrieval_prohibition.enforcement_in_tool_permissions: Enforced mechanically, not only by instruction: the subagent is spawned with WebSearch and WebFetch absent from its tool set, with all MCP tools absent, and with a Bash deny-list that blocks network and dependency-acquisition commands. See 'tool_permissions'.
external_retrieval_prohibition.enforcement_by_audit: After each trial, the orchestrator scans <trial>/logs/agent_tool_calls.jsonl for any denied tool name and for any Bash invocation matching the deny-list patterns. A hit invalidates the trial; it is recorded in _deviations.json with class 'retrieval_violation' and re-run in a fresh context. Violations are published with their counts per language.
external_retrieval_prohibition.documentation_the_model_already_knows: Nothing prevents the model from using knowledge it already has about a language. That is the explicit intent of spec 9: pretraining exposure is deliberately included and Python, C++, Rust and the rest are allowed to benefit from it, while Quidra is evaluated with whatever prior knowledge the model actually has. Only live retrieval is prohibited.

tool_permissions.statement: Every trial subagent, for every one of the ten languages, is spawned with exactly this tool set and exactly these restrictions. Nothing in the tool set names a language, and nothing is added or removed for any language.

allowed_tools.scope: Working directory <trial>/. Subject to the deny-list below. This is what gives the trial compiler, interpreter, and test-runner access.

denied_tools: every artifact, messaging, scheduling, browser, and remote-control tool exposed by the host
tool_permissions.denied_tools_reason: WebSearch/WebFetch/MCP/browser tools would be external retrieval. Task/Workflow/Agent would let a trial spawn further agents and break the single-context, single-trial accounting.
tool_permissions.bash_deny_list_semantics: A Bash command is refused by the harness before execution, per bash_deny_list_matching, if and only if one of its parsed simple commands invokes a denied program or a denied program/subcommand pair. A refusal is recorded as a denied call in agent_tool_calls.jsonl. A refusal is not a trial failure by itself; the trial continues. Repeated attempts are counted and published per language as 'retrieval_attempts', because differing attempt rates across languages are themselves a finding, but they do not change any score.
tool_permissions.path_containment: The trial subagent is given absolute paths only inside <trial>/. Reads outside <trial>/ are refused and logged. The frozen toolchain binaries themselves live outside <trial>/ and are of course executable; this is identical for all ten languages.

compiler_interpreter_test_runner_access.what_the_trial_agent_gets: Bash, with the frozen build and run commands for its target language printed in its system prompt, and the toolchain installed on PATH (with JAVA_HOME pinned to the native arm64 OpenJDK 26 for Java and Kotlin exactly as every other measurement in this run does). The agent may compile, run, re-compile, and re-run its own program as often as it wishes within the trial timeout, and may read the resulting diagnostics in full.
compiler_interpreter_test_runner_access.no_language_gets_more: No language receives a linter, formatter, language server, type checker, test framework, or build system that the frozen recipe in environment.json does not already include, and none is withheld from any language. The recipes are exactly those recorded in environment.json under frozen_toolchain_recipes and used by every other measurement in this run.
compiler_interpreter_test_runner_access.quidra_modes: For Quidra, the trial agent is given the native build/run recipe (quidra build / ./BIN), the same class of recipe every other compiled language receives. The generated Quidra program is additionally executed through the interpreter path (quidra run) by the scoring harness for the raw-results tables required by spec 11 and 29, but the Quidra column of the LLM Practical Effectiveness table uses native mode, matching the release-build treatment given to C++, Rust, Go, Java, Kotlin, Swift and Zig. This is a SELECTION of one mode, not a combination of two; obligation O15 requires publishing Quidra's score recomputed with the interpreter-mode values so the effect of the selection is visible.
compiler_interpreter_test_runner_access.benchmark_harness_access: The trial agent does NOT get the oracle, the golden output file, or the scoring scripts. It gets the behaviour specification and its own program's real output. This is identical for all ten languages. Giving the oracle to the agent would make the task an exercise in reading the answer key.

bash_deny_list_matching._why_not_substring: Substring matching on raw command text produces false denials that correlate with the target language: 'nc' is a substring of func, since, increment, concat and encoding, and 'func' is the function keyword in Go and Swift, so `grep func generated/main.go` would be refused for Go and Swift while the equivalent command is not refused for Python, Java or Quidra. That would break this section's own claim that nothing in the tool set is added or removed for any language. Matching is therefore on parsed argv, never on raw text.
bash_deny_list_matching.procedure: Parse the command with POSIX shell word splitting into a sequence of simple commands, splitting at every pipeline, '&&', '||', ';', newline, and command substitution boundary. For EACH simple command, resolve argv[0], strip any leading environment assignments and any leading 'env', 'sudo', 'command', 'nohup', 'xargs' or 'time' wrapper, and take the basename of argv[0]. Refuse the whole command if any simple command's argv[0] basename is in denied_program_basenames, or if (basename(argv[0]), argv[1]) is in denied_program_subcommand_pairs. Nothing else is matched. A command that cannot be parsed is refused and logged as 'unparseable_command'.
bash_deny_list_matching.denied_module_invocations: A simple command whose argv[0] basename is 'python' or 'python3' and whose argv[1] is '-m' and whose argv[2] is 'pip' is refused. Nothing else about python invocation is matched, because python3 is Python's own frozen run command.
bash_deny_list_matching.explicitly_not_denied: No pattern is matched against a command's arguments, file contents, or any substring of a word. `grep func generated/main.go`, `sed -n '/func main/p' generated/main.go`, `go build -o build/main generated/main.go` and `go run` are all permitted for every language.
bash_deny_list_matching.preflight_required: Before the first scored trial, the matcher is run against a fixed corpus of 50 legitimate commands per language (250 characters max each, covering build, run, grep/sed inspection of the language's own keywords, directory listing, and toolchain --version/--help), authored per language and preserved at llm-practical/config/deny_list_corpus/<language>.txt. The false-denial count per language is published at llm-practical/config/deny_list_false_denials.json. THE DENY LIST IS NOT USABLE AND THE RUN DOES NOT START until that count is zero for all ten languages. The corpus also contains 10 genuinely denied commands per language, which must all be refused, so the matcher is shown to both pass and fail (spec 10.4 item 3).

tool_permissions.bash_deny_list_patterns_legacy_note: The list below is retained ONLY as the human-readable statement of WHICH programs are denied. It is not the matcher. The matcher is bash_deny_list_matching, which parses argv. Any conflict is resolved in favour of bash_deny_list_matching.

exact_system_prompt.text:
You are generating a program for a frozen, adversarial, cross-language benchmark.
You are one trial. Your output is scored mechanically. No human will edit what you write.

TARGET LANGUAGE: {{LANGUAGE_DISPLAY_NAME}}
TOOLCHAIN (frozen, do not change): {{TOOLCHAIN_VERSION}}
SOURCE FILE YOU MUST WRITE: {{WORKDIR}}/generated/{{ENTRY_FILENAME}}
BUILD COMMAND THAT WILL BE USED: {{BUILD_COMMAND}}
RUN COMMAND THAT WILL BE USED: {{RUN_COMMAND}}
REFERENCE MATERIAL SUPPLIED TO YOU: {{WORKDIR}}/pack/

RULES

1. Write exactly one source file, at the path above. Do not create additional source files unless
   the task specification explicitly requires them. Do not modify, move, or delete any file
   outside {{WORKDIR}}/generated/. You may write working files under {{WORKDIR}}/scratch/; nothing
   there is scored, and it is preserved for audit.

2. Use only the target language's standard library and the toolchain as it is installed on this
   machine, EXCEPT the facilities listed as prohibited in your task specification, which you must
   not use even though they are part of your standard library or toolchain. Do not add, download,
   install, vendor, fetch, or generate a third-party dependency, and do not modify any build
   configuration outside the build command shown above.

3. You have no network access and no web, search, or external document retrieval. The only
   reference material you may use is: this prompt, the files under {{WORKDIR}}/pack/, and the
   real diagnostics that the compiler, interpreter, or test runner produces when you build or run
   your own program. Do not attempt to retrieve anything else. Attempting network retrieval
   invalidates this trial.

4. You may build and run your own program as many times as you wish inside {{WORKDIR}}, using the
   build and run commands above. Reading real compiler, interpreter, and runtime output is
   expected, and is the same privilege that every language in this benchmark receives.

5. The program must be deterministic. Given the same input it must produce the same bytes on every
   run, on every execution of the same binary.

6. Print exactly what the task specification asks for and nothing else. Extra output, banners,
   progress messages, or debug lines fail the mechanical oracle.

7. Do not hard-code an answer that the specification asks you to compute. Embedding a precomputed
   result, a lookup table of the expected output, or a branch that detects the benchmark input and
   returns a stored answer is a benchmark violation. It is scored as a failure even when the
   printed bytes match.

8. Write the program the way a competent working developer in this language would write it:
   idiomatic, straightforward, using the language's normal facilities and its normal error
   handling. Do not write deliberately clever, deliberately compressed, deliberately verbose, or
   deliberately minimal code. Do not optimise for source length or for token count.

9. When you are finished, your final message must contain nothing but the single line

   DONE: {{ENTRY_FILENAME}}

   The file on disk is what is scored. Your prose is not scored and is not read by the oracle.

THE TASK FOLLOWS IN THE NEXT MESSAGE.
exact_system_prompt.delivery: Supplied as the spawned subagent's system/instruction message. The task prompt is supplied as the first user message immediately afterwards.
exact_system_prompt.preserved_at: <trial>/prompts/system_prompt.txt, fully substituted, byte-exact, for every trial.
exact_system_prompt.freeze_note: Rules 1 and 2 were amended on 2026-09-18 during pre-registration remediation, BEFORE the first scored generation of this run and before any score was computed from any document of this methodology. The amendment is therefore not a post-result change and does not require a new benchmark run id under amendment_and_freeze_rules. It is recorded in remediation_changelog and in _deviations.json with class 'pre_freeze_amendment'. After the first scored generation this text is immutable.

exact_repair_prompt_template.identical_across_languages_except: the same placeholder set, plus the real diagnostics which are by definition language-specific because they are that language's real toolchain output. The COMPLIANCE RESULT block is present in every repair prompt for every language, filled with its N/A literal when there is nothing to report, so the template's shape never varies by language.

placeholder_fill_rules.{{STAGE}}: Filled from the total mapping table in stage_mapping_is_total. Derived mechanically from the classification of the previous version. No further wording is added.
placeholder_fill_rules.{{BUILD_COMMAND}} / {{BUILD_EXIT_CODE}}: For languages whose frozen recipe has no separate build step (Python), each of these four fields is filled with the literal string 'N/A (this language has no separate build step in its frozen recipe)'. This is a property of the recipe, not a penalty or an advantage, and the same literal is used for every such language.
placeholder_fill_rules.{{RUN_STDOUT}} / {{RUN_STDERR}} / {{RUN_: Verbatim from the frozen run command, truncated per repair_feedback_truncation. If the program was never run because the build failed, each is filled with the literal string 'N/A (the program was not run because the build failed)'.
placeholder_fill_rules.{{TEST_RESULT_SUMMARY}}: The mechanical line 'checks passed: P of T' plus, when applicable, 'exit code: E'. No interpretation, no cause, no hint.
placeholder_fill_rules.{{ORACLE_DIFF}}: The frozen expected-vs-actual rendering described in repair_feedback_truncation. If the oracle was not run because there was no output to compare, the literal string 'N/A (the program did not produce output to compare)'. If every oracle check passed, the literal string 'N/A (every oracle check passed)'.
placeholder_fill_rules.{{COMPLIANCE_SUMMARY}}: The mechanical line 'compliance items satisfied: P of K'. No interpretation, no cause, no hint. If compliance was not evaluated because there was no artefact, the literal string 'N/A (no source file was found at the required path)'.
placeholder_fill_rules.{{COMPLIANCE_FAILING_ITEMS}}: The verbatim ids of the failing compliance items, one per line, in the task's fixed checklist order, with no interpretation and no suggested fix. For a failing anti-hardcoding check the id is accompanied by the verbatim offending literal(s) the check matched, with no comment. If every compliance item was satisfied, the literal string 'N/A (all compliance items were satisfied)'. The block is present byte-identically for all ten languages.

exact_repair_prompt_template.prohibition: The orchestrator must not add any sentence to a repair prompt beyond this template. It must not name a suspected cause, quote a language rule, suggest an API, indicate which line is wrong beyond what the toolchain itself printed, or state how many repair turns have succeeded elsewhere.

stage_mapping_is_total._why: The classifier produces seven classes; the previous enum named four, leaving NO_ARTIFACT, SILENT_BUG and COMPLIANCE_FAIL unmapped and the fill of the build/run/oracle fields undefined in those cases. An undefined fill is a judgement left to whoever runs the orchestrator, and it moves Repair Success (7%), Repair Efficiency (5%) and Diagnosis Efficiency (5%). The mapping below is total and mechanical.

mapping.COMPILE_FAIL: PARSE_OR_COMPILE_FAILED, except subclass BUILD_TIMEOUT which maps to BUILD_TIMED_OUT
mapping.RUNTIME_FAIL: RUNTIME_FAILED, except subclass RUN_TIMEOUT which maps to TIMED_OUT

stage_mapping_is_total.no_other_value: {{STAGE}} takes no value outside this table. The mapping adds no interpretation, names no cause, and is identical for all ten languages.

field_fills_per_stage.NO_SOURCE_FILE_FOUND: Every build, run, oracle and compliance field is filled with the literal string 'N/A (no source file was found at the required path)'.
field_fills_per_stage.COMPLIANCE_FAILED: Build and run fields are filled verbatim as usual. {{TEST_RESULT_SUMMARY}} reads 'checks passed: T of T' because the oracle matched, and {{ORACLE_DIFF}} is 'N/A (every oracle check passed)'. {{COMPLIANCE_SUMMARY}} and {{COMPLIANCE_FAILING_ITEMS}} carry the real compliance result, which is the information the model needs and previously had no field for.

exact_repair_prompt_template.freeze_note: The COMPLIANCE RESULT block and the total stage mapping were added on 2026-09-18 during pre-registration remediation, before the first scored generation and before any score was computed. Recorded in remediation_changelog and in _deviations.json with class 'pre_freeze_amendment'.

per_language_placeholder_substitutions._note: This is the complete and exclusive list of per-language variation permitted in any prompt. Every value is benchmark-controlled and comes from environment.json's frozen_toolchain_recipes or from the fixed table below. BIN, OUT, and FILE are resolved to concrete paths inside the trial directory by the orchestrator.
per_language_placeholder_substitutions.toolchain_api_drift_note: Where methodology/00_cross_language_constraints.md item C-4 records that a frozen toolchain's current API differs from a widely reproduced older idiom (TypeScript 7's removal of --outFile; Zig 0.16's Io-instance stdout), and where subs.harness_configuration_pins records a pinned flag or entry-point convention, the corrective note is supplied to that language's pack in the same slot in which every other language receives its own recipe notes, and the slot exists for all ten languages. It states only the current spelling of the console-output call and the harness's own entry-point convention; it does not supply task logic.

harness_configuration_pins._authority: spec 10.4 pre-flight item (b): harness conventions are satisfied by the harness, not demanded of the model; methodology/00_cross_language_constraints.md C-4.
harness_configuration_pins.TypeScript_target: The frozen TypeScript build command pins --target es2022 --module commonjs. Unpinned, tsc runs at its default target, where BigInt literals and BigInt-typed arithmetic are rejected with 'BigInt literals are not available when targeting lower than ES2020'. UG-03 (2^53 and 2^53+1 exactly) and UG-04 (the minimum signed 64-bit integer and its absolute value exactly) are unrepresentable in a double and require BigInt in TypeScript. Leaving the target unpinned would fail TypeScript two of twelve UG cases (a 6 percent metric) for a harness-configuration reason, which is precisely the class of failure spec 10.4(b) says the harness must absorb. The pin grants TypeScript no capability another language lacks: every one of the other nine already has exact 64-bit or arbitrary-precision integers under its own frozen recipe. environment.json's frozen_toolchain_recipes must carry the identical string.
harness_configuration_pins.Java_Kotlin_entry_point: The build_run_recipe.txt slot, which exists for all ten languages, carries for Java the line 'declare no package; the entry point must be the top-level class Main' and for Kotlin the line 'declare no package; the entry point must be a top-level main function in main.kt'. The frozen recipes `javac -d build generated/Main.java` / `java -cp build Main` and `kotlinc ... -d build/main.jar` / `java -jar build/main.jar` break if the model declares a package, and the system prompt does not forbid one. Stating the harness's own entry-point convention in the recipe slot is the same service every other language already receives from that slot (the C-4 drift notes); it supplies no task logic.
harness_configuration_pins.no_language_specific_task_help: Each pin states a harness convention or a toolchain flag only. None of them states how to solve any task, and none is available to one language as an advantage: they remove harness artefacts that would otherwise be scored as language failures.

Five trials per seed would replicate replication. The Intrinsic track's own configuration document governs its condition set; this document governs the shared engine, prompts, tool permissions, retry, timeout, ordering, and preservation rules, which apply unchanged to it.

reporting_obligation.must_state_executed_counts: results/llm_practical_summary.md and raw/llm_practical_raw.json MUST publish, per (task_id, language) cell, the number of trials ACTUALLY EXECUTED and the number ACTUALLY SCORED, not the number planned. Trials lost to infrastructure exhaustion reduce the executed count and are listed with their reason.
reporting_obligation.precision_statement_required: Every table row whose underlying cells carry fewer than five trials MUST be accompanied by the frozen sentence: 'This row is measured with N trial(s) per language. Differences of a few points between languages are not resolved by this measurement and must not be read as a ranking.' N is the actual count.
reporting_obligation.single_sample_prohibition: A single sample must never be presented as though it carried the precision of five. No confidence interval, significance claim, or ranking claim may be attached to a one-trial cell. Where one trial was run, the run must not describe a few-point difference between languages as a real difference.
reporting_obligation.five_trial_cells_reporting: For the five-trial cells (PE-P1 and the three PR variations) the run publishes, per language, the per-trial outcomes, the resulting rate, and the exact binomial spread (min and max over trials), so readers can see that a five-trial rate has a resolution of 20 percentage points and nothing finer.

resolution_floor.one_trial_cells: 100 percentage points; the measurement distinguishes only pass from fail
resolution_floor.PromptRobustness: COARSER than 20 percentage points. The raw is the MINIMUM of three rates each estimated from 5 trials. The minimum of three binomial estimates is biased LOW relative to the underlying worst-case rate, and the bias is largest for mid-range languages. The attainable value set is {0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100} but the sampling distribution is not the same as that of a single 5-trial rate, and no ranking claim may be attached to a difference of one step.
resolution_floor.Correct@N: 25 percentage points. Four eligible cells, each contributing a binary outcome, so the metric takes only the five values {0, 25, 50, 75, 100}.
resolution_floor.Correct@1_scored: 20 percentage points. The scored Correct@1 is PE-P1-svm-specA alone, five trials.

trial_allocation.deviation_register_obligation: Every cell whose trials_per_language is not five is entered in _deviations.json with class 'trial_count_shortfall', its planned count, and the statement that the spec 6.2 default is five. task_ordering_policy.rule: The full execution schedule is a single fixed permutation of every (task_id, language, trial_index) triple, generated before the first trial and published at llm-practical/trials/_execution_order.json.
task_ordering_policy.generation: Enumerate the triples in ascending lexicographic order of (task_id, language_slug, trial_index). Assign each triple a sort key from the Park-Miller minimal-standard LCG defined in methodology/00_cross_language_constraints.md item C-1 (state_{n+1} = state_n * 48271 mod 2147483647), seeded with 20260917, drawing one value per triple in enumeration order. Sort ascending by (sort_key, task_id, language_slug, trial_index). The result is the execution order.
task_ordering_policy.constraint_applied_after_shuffle: The schedule is then checked to satisfy a language-spread constraint: in any window of ten consecutive scheduled trials, no language may appear more than three times. If the constraint is violated, the smallest-index offending trial is swapped with the next later trial that repairs the violation, repeating until the constraint holds. This repair is deterministic and is recorded step by step in _execution_order.json so a third party reproduces the identical schedule.
task_ordering_policy.why: Each trial runs in a fresh isolated context, so ordering cannot affect a trial's own content. The order is fixed anyway for exact reproducibility, and the spread constraint keeps host thermal state, background load, and any provider-side drift from correlating with a single language, which would otherwise be indistinguishable from a language effect in the timing metrics measured on the generated programs.
task_ordering_policy.resumption: If the run is interrupted, execution resumes at the first schedule index with no completed trial directory. The schedule is never regenerated.
task_ordering_policy.no_reordering_after_results: The schedule must not be regenerated, reshuffled, or extended after any scored output has been observed.

timeout_policy.run_timeout_rationale: Each limit is at least 30x the reference implementation's measured wall-clock on this host for that workload, so it is a hang detector and not a performance threshold. The same absolute limit applies to all ten languages, including the interpreted ones; if a correct program in some language legitimately needs longer than the limit, that is recorded as a TIMEOUT with the measured duration and published, and the limit is not adjusted after the fact.

timeout_classification.build_timeout: Classified as COMPILE_FAIL with subclass BUILD_TIMEOUT. It is a real property of the generated program plus toolchain, not an infrastructure failure.
timeout_classification.run_timeout: Classified as RUNTIME_FAIL with subclass RUN_TIMEOUT. It is NOT a silent bug (the program did not complete), and NOT an infrastructure failure.
timeout_classification.agent_wall_clock_timeout: Split by retry_policy_infrastructure.agent_self_exhaustion_split. Case (a) (no completed model turn or tool call in the last 300 s before the deadline) is an INFRASTRUCTURE event of class 'agent_timeout_stalled' and the retry policy applies. Case (b) (the subagent was still working at the deadline) is NOT infrastructure: it is classified from the artefact on disk by the ordinary ladder, scored, and recorded with subclass 'agent_budget_exhausted'.

timeout_policy.process_supervision: Build and run are executed with a hard kill at the limit (SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 5 s). The measured duration, the signal used, and any partial output are preserved.

retry_policy_infrastructure._authority: spec 6.2: 'Provider failures, rate limits, transport failures, and infrastructure failures must be recorded separately from language/model failures and must not be silently converted into incorrect generations.'
classified_as_language_or_model_failure_: the model produced no file at the required path
the model produced a file that does not parse or compile
the model produced a program that crashes
the model produced a program whose output fails the oracle
the model refused or declined the task
the model produced output the extractor could not resolve to a single source file
the model was still generating or tool-calling when it hit the wall-clock limit (subclass agent_budget_exhausted)
the model was still generating or tool-calling when it filled its context window (subclass agent_budget_exhausted)

agent_self_exhaustion_split._why: Spec 6.2 separates PROVIDER, network, transport and infrastructure failure from language/model failure. A subagent that burns its whole wall-clock budget, or fills its context window, while actively working is exhibiting a model/language outcome, not a provider fault. Treating it as infrastructure would delete a language's hardest failures from the denominator instead of scoring them, and would do so most often for whichever language the model knows least. This rule is stated in language-neutral terms and applies identically to all ten.
applies_to: agent wall-clock timeout on an initial generation or a repair turn
context exhaustion reported by the harness
agent_self_exhaustion_split.mechanical_stall_test: From <trial>/logs/timeline.jsonl and <trial>/logs/agent_tool_calls.jsonl, take the latest timestamp of any completed model turn, any completed tool call, or any streamed-output event for this trial. Let GAP = deadline_timestamp - that timestamp. If GAP >= 300 s, the subagent produced nothing for the last five minutes before the deadline: classify (a). Otherwise classify (b). The threshold is 300 s, frozen, identical for all ten languages, and applied by scripts/classify_exhaustion.py, whose SHA-256 is recorded in the results.
agent_self_exhaustion_split.case_a_stalled: event_class 'agent_timeout_stalled' or 'context_exhausted_stalled'. INFRASTRUCTURE. The trial is discarded, preserved under _aborted/, and retried per retry_rule. It enters no metric.
agent_self_exhaustion_split.case_b_budget_exhausted: subclass 'agent_budget_exhausted'. NOT infrastructure. The trial is NOT retried. Whatever exists at <trial>/generated/ at the deadline is captured, hashed, built, run and classified by the ordinary version_classification_ladder (NO_ARTIFACT when no file exists at the required path, or the class its actual artefact earns). The trial is SCORED and counts in every metric denominator exactly like any other scored trial. If the exhaustion occurred during repair turn k, the trial's final version is the last completed version and repair_turns_used is k.
agent_self_exhaustion_split.no_partial_credit_for_stopping: A trial in case (b) receives no relief of any kind for having run out of budget. Running out of budget is not an excuse the benchmark grants to any language.
agent_self_exhaustion_split.publication: results/llm_infrastructure_events.md publishes, per language, the count of case (a) and the count of case (b) separately, together with the frozen sentence: 'Case (b) counts are agent budget exhaustion. They were SCORED and entered the metrics; they were not treated as infrastructure and were not retried.' The per-trial GAP value and the two source timestamps are preserved in <trial>/logs/exhaustion_split.json so the split can be re-derived by a third party.

retry_policy_infrastructure.retry_rule: On an infrastructure event (and only on an infrastructure event, i.e. case (a) of agent_self_exhaustion_split and the provider/transport/host classes) the trial is discarded in full (its partial directory is moved to <trial>/../_aborted/<trial_id>.<attempt>/ and preserved) and retried from a fresh isolated context with the byte-identical prompt. Up to 3 retries per trial. A case (b) agent-budget exhaustion is never retried.
retry_policy_infrastructure.exhaustion: If all attempts fail, the cell records one fewer executed trial. If a cell ends with zero executed trials, every metric that depends on that cell is marked N/A for that language with reason 'infrastructure_exhausted' and renormalised per spec 26, and the shortfall is published in _deviations.json and repeated in the results summary. It is never scored as a failure of the language or of the model.
retry_policy_infrastructure.recording: Every infrastructure event, including every retried attempt, is appended to llm-practical/trials/_infrastructure_events.jsonl with fields: timestamp_utc, task_id, language, trial_index, attempt, event_class, stall_gap_seconds, provider_message_verbatim, action_taken, aborted_dir. Case (b) agent-budget exhaustions are recorded in the same file with action_taken='scored_not_retried' so both sides of the split are visible in one place. The per-language counts of both cases are published in results/llm_infrastructure_events.md so a reader can see that no language absorbed more infrastructure noise than another, and that no language's self-exhaustion was absorbed as infrastructure.
retry_policy_infrastructure.prohibition: An infrastructure event must never be written into a versions/ directory as a failed generation, must never fill an oracle result, and must never be counted in Generation Success Rate, Compile Success Rate, Correct@1, or any other metric denominator.

reference_and_specification_pack_policy.principle: Spec 9 permits a specification-assisted condition as the normal practical prompt. Every language therefore receives a reference pack of a matched budget, built by one mechanical rule. Quidra receives no more and no less than the others. The packs are built and their token counts published before the first scored trial.

pack_contents_identical_slots.budget: 20,000 tokens by the frozen counter, for every language

The slot exists for all ten languages; for languages with no drift note the file carries the literal line 'no toolchain API drift notes for this language'.

reference_and_specification_pack_policy.selection_rule_for_language_reference: Take the language's single official reference document as pinned in packs/pack_sources.json (URL or local path, plus SHA-256 of the exact bytes used, fetched once before the run and never during a trial). Split it into sections at its top-level headings, in document order. Emit sections in document order until adding the next section would exceed 20,000 tokens by the frozen counter; stop there. Truncation is never mid-section. The identical procedure, budget, and stopping rule is applied to all ten languages. No section is chosen because it helps or hurts a language, and no section is reordered. IDENTICAL PROCEDURE IS NOT IDENTICAL INFORMATION VALUE: see coverage_asymmetry_disclosure below.
reference_and_specification_pack_policy.quidra_pack: Quidra's language_reference.md is produced by exactly this rule from Quidra 0.2.0's own official reference documentation, pinned by SHA-256 like every other. If Quidra's reference is shorter than 20,000 tokens, the whole document is used and the shortfall is published as a raw number; the budget is not topped up with additional Quidra material, and no other language's budget is cut to match. The resulting coverage asymmetry is disclosed under coverage_asymmetry_disclosure and published under O14, because a rule that is identical in procedure is not identical in the information it delivers.
reference_and_specification_pack_policy.no_specification_diagnostic: DIAG-NOPACK-svm-specA supplies task_spec.md and build_run_recipe.txt but NO language_reference.md and NO examples/, for all ten languages identically. Its results are a diagnostic of prior knowledge only and are never folded into any score (spec 9).

counters_published: frozen_lexical_counter (defined in source_token_counting; the scoring counter)

harness_reported_prompt_tokens (recorded when the harness reports input-token usage for the trial; this is the model's own tokenizer and is published beside the lexical count, never substituted for it)
token_count_publication.obligation: If any language's pack total deviates from the ten-language median by more than 15 percent, the deviation and its cause are published in the results summary. The packs are NOT rebalanced after the fact; the budget rule is fixed and its residual differences are reported rather than hidden.

reference_and_specification_pack_policy.pack_immutability: Packs are built once, hashed, and made read-only before the first scored trial. <trial>/pack/ is a copy; its SHA-256 manifest is written to <trial>/prompts/pack_manifest.json and re-verified at scoring.

coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.statement: A fixed document-order budget delivers very different FRACTIONS of different languages' definitions. A language whose official reference is shorter than 20,000 tokens receives 100 percent of it. A language whose reference is very long - the Python Language Reference, the C++ working paper, the Rust reference, the Java Language Specification, the Swift book - receives a document-order PREFIX of a few percent, and for several of them the first 20,000 tokens are lexical structure and the object/data model rather than the material needed to write a numerical program. The nine incumbent languages are expected to fall back on pretraining, which is spec 9's explicit intent; but the combination means the language with the LEAST pretraining exposure may be the only one holding a complete definition, and the residual tilts in its favour on every metric.
coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.quidra_specific_consequence: On this run's pinned sources, Quidra 0.2.0's official reference is expected to fit inside the budget in full, so Quidra is the language most likely to receive 100 percent coverage. That is a real asymmetry produced by a neutral rule, and it is disclosed rather than corrected.
coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.what_is_not_done: The rule is frozen and is NOT changed after freeze: the budget is not cut for Quidra, not topped up for anyone, and no per-language coverage correction factor is invented. Spec 7 additionally forbids discounting an established language's real ecosystem, tooling and maturity advantage as an 'incumbency effect'; the symmetric obligation is not to let a documentation-coverage advantage run the other way undisclosed.
coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.reporting_obligation: O14. The coverage figures are already published fields (language_reference_sections_included, language_reference_sections_available, and the token counts); O14 requires them beside the main table with the frozen sentence.
coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.symmetry_test: The obligation is written in terms of sections_included / sections_available for all ten. Had Zig's or Go's reference been the short one, the identical disclosure would name that language.

examples_budget.rule: Every language receives the same NUMBER of worked examples and the same example ROLES. The bytes differ because the languages differ; nothing else differs.
fixed_example_roles_for_the_3_example_bu: E1. A complete, buildable, runnable program that prints one fixed line of text and exits successfully. Demonstrates the entry point, the console-output call, and program termination.
E2. A complete program that iterates a fixed array or list of 5 integers, sums them, and prints the sum. Demonstrates a sequence type, iteration, and integer output.
E3. A complete program that prints one fixed floating-point value formatted to exactly 6 decimal places. Demonstrates fixed-precision numeric formatting, which every task's oracle depends on.
fixed_example_roles_for_the_6_example_bu: E1, E2, E3 as above, plus:
E4. A complete program that defines a function taking two integers and returning one, and prints its result for one fixed argument pair. Demonstrates function definition and call.
E5. A complete program that builds a key-to-integer mapping with 3 fixed entries and prints one looked-up value. Demonstrates an associative collection.

E6. A complete program that attempts ONE specified failing operation, handles the failure using the language's normal error-handling facility, prints the literal text 'handled', and exits successfully. THE SPECIFIED FAILING OPERATION IS: open for reading the file at the relative path './e6_absent_file_do_not_create.txt', which the harness guarantees does not exist in the example directory or in any trial directory. This operation was chosen because it is expressible with normal facilities and its failure is detectable and recoverable in all ten languages without exceptions being required: an error union in Zig, a Result in Rust, an (err != nil) return in Go, a throwing call in Swift, Java, Kotlin, Python, TypeScript and Quidra, and a stream state check in C++. It deliberately differs from the failing operations the UG task asks about (integer division by zero in UG-09, base-10 parsing of '12x' in UG-10), so E6 does not demonstrate either of them.
authoring_rules: Each example is written by the benchmark authors, not by the model, and is verified to build and run with the frozen recipe before the run starts.
No example demonstrates anything a task asks the model to compute. Examples show language mechanics only.

Examples for different languages must express the same role and nothing more. An example may not incidentally demonstrate a second mechanic in one language that another language's example does not demonstrate.

Size matching: each example's lexical token count must lie within a factor of 2 of the ten-language median for that example role. Where a language cannot meet that because its minimal expression of the role is genuinely longer or shorter, the residual is published per language in packs/example_token_counts.json and is NOT corrected by padding or trimming.
The complete set of examples for all ten languages is preserved at llm-practical/packs/<language>/examples/ and hashed.
examples_budget.for_quidra: Quidra's six example roles are authored by the same rule and reviewed against the same size-matching constraint. Quidra receives no additional tutorial material, no extra commentary in its examples, and no annotation that another language's examples do not carry.
examples_budget.e6_operation_neutrality_note: An operation whose failure is non-catchable in some of the ten (integer division by zero, out-of-bounds indexing under a release build) would have made the role inexpressible for those languages and would have forced a per-language substitution, which the identical-roles rule forbids. The chosen operation is expressible and recoverable in all ten with each language's own normal facility, and no language needs a workaround.

practical_effectiveness_task_set._principle: Every task is specified by required observable behaviour only. No task statement names a language, a type, an operator, a standard-library symbol, or a syntax. Every oracle is a mechanical program comparison with no human judgement. The same task_spec.md bytes go to all ten languages.

common_task_contract.program_shape: One source file at generated/<ENTRY_FILENAME>. The program reads nothing from stdin unless the task says otherwise, takes no command-line arguments, prints its result lines to stdout in the specified order, and exits with status 0 on success.
common_task_contract.determinism: All pseudo-random data is produced by the Park-Miller minimal-standard LCG frozen in methodology/00_cross_language_constraints.md item C-1: state_{n+1} = (state_n * 48271) mod 2147483647, seed stated per task, unit float = state_{n+1} / 2147483647.0. The task specification states this generator in words and formulas, identically for all ten languages. It is exactly representable in every one of the ten languages; no language needs a workaround and none gets a shortcut.
common_task_contract.float_formatting: Every floating-point value printed by a task is printed with exactly the number of decimal places the task states, using round-half-away-from-zero at that decimal place, with a leading '-' for negative values and no thousands separators, no exponent form, and no locale formatting. Negative zero is printed as if it were positive zero. This rule is stated in every task_spec.md verbatim and is the same for all ten languages (methodology/00 item C-2).
common_task_contract.no_extra_output: Any stdout line beyond those specified fails the oracle. Anything the language runtime writes to stderr does not fail the oracle by itself, but is recorded and is used by the silent-bug and hallucination classifiers.
common_task_contract.line_endings: Lines are separated by LF. A single trailing LF at end of output is accepted; CRLF is not. The oracle strips exactly one trailing LF from both expected and actual before comparison and compares the remainder byte for byte.
common_task_contract.compliance_checklist: Each task ships a fixed list of K binary, mechanically checkable requirements in task_spec.md, checked by scripts/check_compliance.py using the observable predicates in compliance_predicates. The checker's logic is identical for all languages; its only per-language input is the entry filename and the frozen build/run recipe.

numeric_tolerance_policy._authority: methodology/frozen_tolerance.json, tolerance_id ALGO-TOL-1, defined in methodology/07_algorithm_workloads.md section 1.6; methodology/00_cross_language_constraints.md C-2.
numeric_tolerance_policy.adopted_verbatim: PE-P1 through PE-P6 use ALGO-TOL-1 verbatim. The LLM track does not define its own, tighter tolerance for the same algorithms.

numeric_match.predicate: abs(actual - golden) <= max( abs + rel * abs(golden), print_ulp[field_kind] )

numeric_tolerance_policy.why_the_earlier_figures_were_withdrawn: This document previously froze abs 1e-06 OR rel 1e-09 for PE-P1 and abs 1e-05 OR rel 1e-08 for PE-P3, with abs and rel transposed relative to the run's own frozen figure and with no print_ulp floor. For a GMM log-likelihood of magnitude ~1e4 that is roughly a hundred times tighter than ALGO-TOL-1. Its stated rationale ('the condition number keeps every printed field stable well inside 1e-06') was asserted and never measured, and is contradicted by ALGO-TOL-1's own measured rationale that rel 1e-6 is needed to absorb FMA contraction under the frozen build recipes and the per-runtime differences in log/exp/sqrt across ten toolchains. Because every golden file is produced by the C++ reference on this host, a tolerance tighter than real cross-toolchain libm variation makes the other nine languages pay for differences from C++'s libm. Adopting ALGO-TOL-1 removes that advantage; it does not create one for anybody.
numeric_tolerance_policy.print_ulp_floor_why: The output contract quantizes to a fixed number of decimal places. Two correct implementations may legitimately print adjacent last digits, and that difference must never be scored as an error. The floor is the same for all ten languages.
numeric_tolerance_policy.no_post_hoc_change: No score has been computed from any document of this methodology, so this alignment is pre-registration, not post-result formula selection. After the first scored generation the tolerance is immutable.

exact_match_integer_field_preflight._why: PE-P1's support-vector count and correct-classification count, PE-P3's iteration count and hard-assignment counts, and any other discrete field are compared for EXACT equality. SMO over its frozen sweep budget and EM over its frozen iteration budget can turn a 1-ulp difference into a different working-set selection or a different convergence step, which would make an exact-match integer field non-reproducible across toolchains for reasons unrelated to correctness. An exact-match field that is not stable is an instrument defect, and it would fall hardest on whichever languages' runtimes differ most from the C++ reference that produced the golden.
exact_match_integer_field_preflight.required_before_freezing_any_golden: For each of PE-P1, PE-P3 and PE-P5, the benchmark authors implement the workload's reference in AT LEAST THREE of the ten languages, chosen to span a compiled-native, a managed and a dynamically typed runtime, build and run all three under the frozen recipes on this host, and confirm that (i) every float field agrees within ALGO-TOL-1 and (ii) EVERY exact-match integer field agrees exactly across all three.
exact_match_integer_field_preflight.if_an_integer_field_is_unstable: It is removed from the exact-match set, or the workload is reparameterised so that it is stable, BEFORE the golden file is frozen and before the first scored trial. It is never left in the exact-match set with a caveat, and it is never relaxed after a trial has run.
exact_match_integer_field_preflight.published: The three implementations, their outputs, and the per-field agreement table are preserved at llm-practical/tasks/<task_id>/preflight_stability/ and hashed. The reference languages used are recorded; none of them gains anything from being used, because the model is never shown them for PE-P1/P3/P5.
exact_match_integer_field_preflight.blocks_the_run: Readiness item C3 is not satisfied until this pre-flight passes for every task that has an exact-match integer field.

compliance_predicates._why: A compliance item is worth part of a 7 percent metric and must be mechanically checkable from what the program does, not from a judgement about what the agent did. Three of PE-P1's items had no stated detection method and one of them ('no file written outside build/') contradicted tool_permissions, which grants the trial agent Write and Edit on <trial>/scratch/: an agent using the scratch directory it was explicitly given would have failed a compliance item. Every item below is a predicate on the program under the frozen run command, identical in logic for all ten languages.
compliance_predicates.no_file_written_outside_build: The harness records the set of filesystem paths created or modified DURING the frozen run command (by snapshotting <trial>/ before and after and comparing path, size and mtime). The item fails if that set contains any path outside <trial>/build/. Files the agent wrote at authoring time, including everything under <trial>/scratch/ and <trial>/generated/, are OUT OF SCOPE of this item: the item is about the program's behaviour, not the agent's workspace.
compliance_predicates.no_stdin_read: Run the frozen run command twice: once with stdin connected to /dev/null, once with stdin connected to a 1 MiB stream of fixed bytes (0x41 repeated, produced by the harness). The item passes if stdout is byte-identical between the two runs and the exit status is the same. No source is searched and no per-language symbol list is used.
compliance_predicates.no_command_line_arguments_consulted: Run the frozen run command once as frozen and once with three extra arguments appended ('--benchmark-ignored-a', '--benchmark-ignored-b', '--benchmark-ignored-c'). The item passes if stdout is byte-identical between the two runs and the exit status is the same.
compliance_predicates.determinism: Run the frozen run command three times. The item passes if all three stdout streams are byte-identical.
compliance_predicates.float_decimal_places: Each field the schema types as F6 must match the regular expression '^-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]{6}$' and each F12 field '^-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]{12}$', checked on the printed bytes.
compliance_predicates.lcg_seed_used: Replaces the previous item, which described no implementable check. Each task's oracle_schema carries one named field that is a direct function of the generator stream and of nothing else: for PE-P1 the field id is LCG_PROBE_U5, defined as the 5th unit float of the frozen LCG at the task's stated seed, printed to 12 decimals. The item passes if and only if that field matches the golden value exactly under the F12 predicate. The field is part of the specified output for all ten languages and is stated in the byte-identical task_spec.md; it is not a debug channel.
compliance_predicates.applies_identically: These predicates are implemented once in scripts/check_compliance.py and run unchanged for all ten languages. Their only per-language inputs are the entry filename and the frozen build/run recipe.

tasks.role: PRIMARY implementation task. Correct@1 is measured here.
tasks.scenario: A (spec 16 A). The reference source code is NOT shown.
supplied: algorithm specification in words and formulas
tasks.workload_summary: Train a soft-margin linear support vector machine by sequential minimal optimisation on a deterministic two-class dataset generated by the frozen LCG (seed 1), with the dimensionality, sample count, class separation, penalty parameter C, tolerance and maximum passes fixed in tasks/PE-P1-svm-specA/workload.json. Then classify a deterministic held-out set generated by the same LCG continuing from the training stream. Print, in this fixed order: the number of support vectors; the bias term to 6 decimals; each weight component to 6 decimals, one per line; the number of correctly classified held-out samples; and the held-out accuracy to 6 decimals.

steps: 1. Build with the frozen build command. Non-zero exit or absent binary => COMPILE_FAIL.
2. Run with the frozen run command, run_timeout 120 s. Non-zero exit, killing signal, or timeout => RUNTIME_FAIL.
3. Parse stdout into the fixed field schema in tasks/PE-P1-svm-specA/oracle_schema.json. A line count or field shape that does not match the schema => OUTPUT_MISMATCH.

4. Compare integer fields (support-vector count, correct-classification count) for EXACT equality with the golden file. Each such field must first have passed common_task_contract.exact_match_integer_field_preflight.
5. Compare floating-point fields (bias, each weight component, accuracy) against the golden file under ALGO-TOL-1 (see common_task_contract.numeric_tolerance_policy).
6. PASS if and only if every field matches. Otherwise OUTPUT_MISMATCH.

float_tolerance.rule: A field matches if abs(actual - golden) <= max( 1e-09 + 1e-06 * abs(golden), print_ulp[field_kind] ). This is methodology/frozen_tolerance.json ALGO-TOL-1 adopted verbatim; it is the same tolerance every other measurement of WL-SVM in this run uses, and it is the same for all ten languages.
float_tolerance.rationale: See common_task_contract.numeric_tolerance_policy. rel 1e-6 absorbs FMA contraction under the frozen build recipes and the per-runtime differences in log/exp/sqrt implementations across ten toolchains; it is far tighter than any genuine algorithmic error, which shows up at 1e-2 or larger in every failure mode observed in the reference algorithms.

oracle.pass_fail: Binary. There is no partial credit for Correct@1. Partial credit exists only in Test Pass Rate, which is checks_passed / checks_total over the schema fields.

anti_hardcoding_check._why_rewritten: The previous text turned on an undefined judgement ('not derivable as a task-specified constant') and stated two incompatible procedures at once: auto-FAIL, and human review of the hit list. Which one ran decided scores, and the human-review branch would have injected human judgement into a pipeline this document elsewhere insists is mechanical.
anti_hardcoding_check.numeric_literal_exemption: A numeric literal in the generated source is EXEMPT if and only if it satisfies one of: (i) its normalised decimal text appears verbatim in that task's task_spec.md; (ii) it is one of 0, 1, 2, -1, 0.5; (iii) it is one of the frozen LCG constants 48271 and 2147483647. Normalisation strips underscores, digit separators and a leading '+', lower-cases any exponent marker, and renders the value in plain decimal. Nothing else is exempt, and 'derivable as a task-specified constant' is no longer a criterion anywhere.
anti_hardcoding_check.what_is_searched: The tokenised source. (a) Every non-exempt numeric literal is compared, rounded to the number of decimals the golden field is printed at, against every floating-point field of the golden file; an equality is a hit. (b) Every string literal is compared for equality against every line of the golden output file; an equality is a hit. (c) Every non-exempt integer literal is compared against every integer field of the golden file; an equality is a hit.
anti_hardcoding_check.single_procedure: A hit sets the compliance item 'no hard-coded golden values' to fail and the version's classification to COMPLIANCE_FAIL, mechanically and with NO human review, regardless of output match. There is no second procedure and no override.
anti_hardcoding_check.audit_not_override: The hit list, with each offending literal and its source position, is preserved at <trial>/versions/<version>/anti_hardcoding_hits.json so a third party can audit the RULE. A false positive is reported in _deviations.json with class 'anti_hardcoding_false_positive' and is NOT overturned within this run. Publishing a rule's false positives is not the same as letting a human reverse a score.
anti_hardcoding_check.preflight: Before the first scored trial, the check is run against the benchmark's own reference implementation of the task in at least three of the ten languages and must produce ZERO hits. A non-zero count means the exemption set is wrong and must be corrected before freezing, not after a trial has run. The check is additionally run against a deliberately hard-coded fixture in the same three languages and must produce a hit in each, so the validator is shown to both pass and fail (spec 10.4 item 3). Results preserved at llm-practical/config/anti_hardcoding_validation.json.
anti_hardcoding_check.identical_for_all_ten: Byte-identical logic and byte-identical exemption set for all ten languages. The only per-language input is the comment syntax used by the tokenizer.

delegation_detecting_oracle_fields._why: A first-order gradient is the same number whichever engine computes it, so 'forward values plus first-order gradients' cannot tell a hand-built tape from a delegated one. The fields below are the ones methodology 07 section 4.4 and 4.7 pin precisely because they discriminate. They are scored fields of PE-P5's oracle_schema, not commentary, so a delegated engine fails numerically and not only by inspection.

fields.discriminates: Second-order derivative. It is obtainable only if gradient accumulation itself builds graph nodes (07 section 4.4 consequence 1). An engine that accumulates gradients as raw numbers returns 0.000000 here while every first-order field is right.
Mixed second-order derivative; same mechanism as above.
Third-order derivative; requires the backward pass to be differentiable to depth three.

The mul(h, h) double-visit case of 07 section 4.7: the SAME tensor is an input to a binary op twice, so a plain recursive creator walk with no topological sort and no visited set visits it twice and adds its gradient contribution twice, which is the correct answer. Any engine that deduplicates by a visited set or a topological sort contributes it once and every STRESS_* field shifts.
Same double-visit case after 50 SGD steps; the divergence compounds.
Same, at the final extra forward pass.

Step-0 element-0 gradient of P, closed form 2*P0*(Q0+1)^2 = 0.282227 (07 section 4.7). Checked against the closed form as well as against golden, so backward correctness is established independently of any single implementation.
Step-0 element-0 gradient of Q, closed form 2*P0^2*(Q0+1) = 0.033203.

delegation_detecting_oracle_fields.scored: These fields are part of oracle_schema.json for PE-P5 and PE-P6 and are compared under the same frozen tolerance as every other float field. They are not a separate gate and carry no extra weight; they are ordinary scored fields of the task.
delegation_detecting_oracle_fields.applies_to_all_ten: Every language's implementation must reproduce these fields. Nothing here is specific to any language: an implementation in any of the ten that hand-builds the tape as 07 section 4.4 specifies reproduces them, and an implementation in any of the ten that delegates does not.

Under the unamended rule 2 ('standard library only') Quidra's built-in neural namespace would have satisfied this workload by a call while the other nine hand-built a tape; that asymmetry is removed here.

prohibited_per_language.Quidra: The entire 'neural' namespace in any form (neural.track, neural.grad, neural.Parameter, neural.State, neural.Gradients, neural.mean, every differentiable reduction, neural.save, neural.load) and the entire 'dnn' package.
prohibited_per_language.Python: torch, jax, autograd, tensorflow, numpy, sympy, and any module providing differentiation, tensor or linear-algebra primitives.
prohibited_per_language.C++: Any autodiff, tensor or linear-algebra library, first-party or third-party (including Eigen, Blaze, autodiff, Stan Math, and any BLAS/LAPACK binding).
prohibited_per_language.Rust: Any autodiff, tensor or linear-algebra crate (including ndarray, nalgebra, candle, burn, autodiff, dfdx).
prohibited_per_language.Go: Any autodiff, tensor or linear-algebra package (including gonum, gorgonia).
prohibited_per_language.Java: Any autodiff, tensor or linear-algebra library (including DL4J/ND4J, EJML, Apache Commons Math linear algebra).
prohibited_per_language.TypeScript: Any autodiff or tensor library (including tensorflow.js, ml-matrix).
prohibited_per_language.Kotlin: Any autodiff, tensor or linear-algebra library, including anything reachable from the JVM classpath.
prohibited_per_language.Swift: Any autodiff or tensor facility, including Swift's own differentiable-programming attributes and @differentiable / valueWithGradient / Differentiable conformances, Accelerate, BNNS, and Core ML.
prohibited_per_language.Zig: Any autodiff, tensor or linear-algebra package, and any C interop to one.

prohibited_facilities.explicitly_still_available_to_all_ten: General-purpose numeric facilities that are not differentiation: arithmetic, arrays, dynamic containers, hash maps, sorting, string formatting, sqrt and exp. These remain available to all ten equally.
prohibited_facilities.delivered_to_the_model_how: The prohibition is stated in the BYTE-IDENTICAL task_spec.md for PE-P5 and PE-P6 as a single section listing all ten languages' prohibited facilities, so every language's trial agent reads the same text and sees that the restriction is symmetric. System-prompt rule 2 points at it.
prohibited_facilities.enforcement_compliance_item: scripts/check_compliance.py checks the fixed compliance item 'implemented the differentiation engine in the workload source using general-purpose facilities only' against a frozen per-language banned-symbol list at llm-practical/config/lightgrad_banned_symbols.json (one list per language, hashed, frozen before the first scored trial, derived directly from prohibited_per_language). The check is applied to the tokenised source: a hit on an import/use/include/namespace reference to a banned symbol sets the item to fail and the version's classification to COMPLIANCE_FAIL. The hit list is preserved for audit; a false positive is reported in _deviations.json and is not overturned within this run.
prohibited_facilities.enforcement_numerical: A source-text check alone would be evidence by inspection. The PE-P5 oracle schema therefore also carries scored fields that a delegated engine does not reproduce, listed in delegation_detecting_oracle_fields below.
