tasks.name: Unseen-case Generalization
tasks.design: The pack supplies PART of the language reference (the frozen 20,000-token excerpt) and a LIMITED number of examples (exactly 6, the fixed roles E1-E6). The task then requires twelve cases that the six examples do not demonstrate. Two cases sit in each of the six categories spec 21 names.
tasks.output_contract: The program prints exactly twelve lines, in order, each of the form 'UG-NN: <value>' with NN from 01 to 12 and a single space after the colon.

cases.requirement: Take state_10 of the frozen LCG, i.e. the 10th STATE produced by the recurrence state_{n+1} = (state_n * 48271) mod 2147483647 starting from state_0 = 1 (so state_1 = 48271). Reduce state_10 modulo 97 with both operands positive, giving a result in [0, 96]. Then clamp that result into the inclusive range [-50, 50]. Print the clamped integer.
cases.unseen_because: the examples show iteration and arithmetic separately but never a modulus combined with a signed clamp
cases.fixed_inputs: state_0 = 1; the value used is state_10 = 1596680831.
cases.disclosed_residual: state_10 mod 97 = 12, which already lies inside [-50, 50], so the clamp is INERT at this input. This is disclosed rather than corrected: changing the case's inputs so that the clamp bites would be a workload change, and the rule against altering a task after freeze applies whether or not the change would help any particular language. The case still scores the modulus-with-signed-clamp combination as written, and it is inert identically for all ten languages.

cases.requirement: Fold the first 16 unit floats of the frozen LCG (seed 1) with an alternating rule: add the value at even positions (0-based), subtract it at odd positions. Print the result to 6 decimals.
cases.unseen_because: the examples show summation but never a position-dependent alternating fold
cases.fixed_inputs: the first 16 unit floats of the frozen LCG at seed 1, i.e. unit_k = state_k / 2147483647.0 for k = 1..16; positions are 0-based over that sequence, so unit_1 is at position 0 (added), unit_2 at position 1 (subtracted), and so on.

cases.requirement: Print the exact decimal representations of 2^53 and 2^53+1, separated by a single space.
cases.unseen_because: the examples never touch the exactness boundary of binary floating point
cases.fixed_inputs: the two integers 2^53 and 2^53+1, stated in task_spec.md as 9007199254740992 and 9007199254740993; neither is to be computed in binary64.

cases.requirement: Print the exact decimal representation of the minimum signed 64-bit integer, then a single space, then the exact decimal representation of its absolute value.
cases.unseen_because: the examples never touch the asymmetry of two's-complement range
cases.fixed_inputs: the minimum signed 64-bit integer -9223372036854775808 and its absolute value 9223372036854775808, stated in task_spec.md; the second is outside the signed 64-bit range in every language.

cases.requirement: Evaluate the fully parenthesised six-level nested arithmetic-and-conditional expression over the fixed integer inputs, using signed 64-bit integer arithmetic with division truncating toward zero, and print the integer result.
cases.unseen_because: the examples contain no expression deeper than two levels
cases.fixed_inputs: a = 7, b = 3, c = 11, d = 2, e = 5. The expression, written out in task_spec.md byte-identically for all ten languages, is: ( ( ( ( ( ( a + b ) * c ) - ( d * e ) ) / ( b + d ) ) + ( IF ( ( a * d ) > c ) THEN ( c - b ) ELSE ( b - c ) ) ) * ( e - d ) ). IF/THEN/ELSE denotes a value-producing conditional; each language expresses it with its own normal conditional facility. All intermediate values are exact in signed 64-bit and the one division is exact, so the truncation rule never has to break a tie.

cases.requirement: Build the nested structure described in task_spec.md, an ORDERED mapping from three fixed keys to sequences of key-value pairs, preserving the stated key order (not sorted), then print its specified deterministic serialisation.
cases.unseen_because: example E5 shows a flat mapping only
cases.fixed_inputs: Keys in this order: 'alpha', 'beta', 'gamma'. alpha -> [ ('x',1), ('y',2) ]; beta -> [ ('z',3) ]; gamma -> [ ('p',4), ('q',5), ('r',6) ]. Serialisation: each key is rendered as <key>:{<k1>=<v1>;<k2>=<v2>;...} with inner pairs in the order given and joined by ';'; the three key groups are joined by ','. No spaces anywhere.

cases.requirement: For the three fixed integer pairs in task_spec.md, print the quotient of the pair computed in floating point to 6 decimals, then a single space, then the first element rendered as a decimal string zero-padded to width 12; the three results separated by ' | '.
cases.unseen_because: the examples show integer output and float formatting but never a mixed-type combination or width padding
cases.fixed_inputs: The three integer pairs, in this order: (7, 3), (22, -7), (1000003, 17). The first element of every pair is non-negative, so the width-12 zero-padded rendering never has to place a sign.

cases.requirement: For the eight fixed float values in task_spec.md, print on one line their conversions to integer by truncation toward zero, then ' | ', then their conversions by round-half-away-from-zero; values within each group separated by single spaces.
cases.unseen_because: the examples never convert float to integer and never contrast two rounding rules
cases.fixed_inputs: The eight float values, in this order: 2.5, -2.5, 3.7, -3.7, 0.5, -0.5, 9.99, -9.99. Each is exactly the binary64 value nearest the written decimal. Truncation is toward zero; round-half-away-from-zero is the rule already fixed in common_task_contract.float_formatting. An integer result of zero is printed as '0' with no sign.

cases.requirement: Attempt or guard the integer division of the two fixed operands given in task_spec.md, which are 1 and 0. The failure must be detected and reported; print exactly 'ERROR:DIVZERO'. The program must continue and print the remaining cases and exit with status 0. A conforming implementation may EITHER attempt the division and handle the resulting failure, OR test the divisor and report the failure without attempting it; both satisfy this case. What is scored is the printed line ERROR:DIVZERO, the continuation, and exit status 0.
cases.unseen_because: example E6 shows error handling for a different, specified failing operation
cases.why_both_forms_are_accepted: Integer division by zero is undefined behaviour in C++ and normally delivers SIGFPE, which cannot be caught portably and from which the program cannot continue; it is a non-catchable fatal error in Swift, illegal behaviour in Zig, and a panic in Rust recoverable only through the non-idiomatic catch_unwind. Requiring the trap form would fail four languages for their fault model rather than for their ability to detect and report the condition, and would hand a free pass to the languages whose checked division is catchable. Accepting either form asks all ten the same question: does the program detect the condition, report it in the specified way, and carry on.

cases.requirement: Attempt to interpret the fixed text '12x' as a base-10 integer. The failure must be detected and reported; print exactly 'ERROR:PARSE'. The program must continue and exit with status 0.
cases.unseen_because: the examples never parse text into a number
cases.fixed_inputs: the text '12x' (three ASCII characters, U+0031 U+0032 U+0078), base 10.

cases.requirement: Sort the fixed twelve text-and-integer pairs in task_spec.md by integer descending, ties broken by text ascending in codepoint order, and print them as 'text=integer' joined by ','.
cases.unseen_because: the examples show no sorting and no multi-key comparison
cases.fixed_inputs: The twelve text-and-integer pairs, in this input order: ('delta',5), ('alpha',9), ('echo',5), ('bravo',2), ('golf',9), ('charlie',7), ('hotel',2), ('india',7), ('juliet',1), ('kilo',5), ('lima',9), ('mike',1). All texts are lower-case ASCII, so codepoint order and byte order coincide.

cases.requirement: Count the occurrences of each Unicode codepoint in the fixed text given in task_spec.md, which contains non-ASCII codepoints, and print 'U+XXXX=count' entries in ascending codepoint order, joined by ','. XXXX is at least four uppercase hexadecimal digits with no prefix zeros beyond four.
cases.unseen_because: the examples show no text processing and no codepoint handling
cases.fixed_inputs: The text is given in task_spec.md as an explicit CODEPOINT SEQUENCE, not as raw bytes, so no source-file encoding question can affect it: U+0041, U+00E9, U+0041, U+263A, U+00E9, U+0041 (six codepoints). Counting is over Unicode codepoints, not over UTF-8 bytes and not over UTF-16 code units; every codepoint here is in the Basic Multilingual Plane, so the two-channel distinction cannot silently change the answer for a UTF-16-based runtime.

tasks.fairness_statement: None of the twelve cases was chosen because Quidra handles it well. UG-03, UG-04 and UG-08 sit where Quidra's overflow-checked integer arithmetic makes the case harder rather than easier, and they stay in the set. UG-09 is NOT such a case and the earlier claim that it was has been withdrawn as inaccurate: a language whose checked division raises a catchable error passes UG-09 naturally, while C++, Swift and Zig cannot use the trap form at all, so the case as originally written favoured Quidra rather than burdening it. UG-09 now accepts either the attempt-and-handle form or the guard form, which asks all ten the same question. Every case is expressible in all ten languages using each language's normal facilities.
tasks.oracle: Mechanical, per case: the actual line 'UG-NN: <value>' must equal the golden line byte for byte after the common trailing-LF rule. UG-01, UG-02, UG-03, UG-04, UG-05, UG-06, UG-07, UG-08, UG-09, UG-10, UG-11 and UG-12 have their expected values written into this document and must equal the frozen golden file. A missing, extra, or out-of-order line scores that case FAIL and does not shift the others: comparison is by case id, not by position, and an out-of-order or duplicated id fails the affected ids.
tasks.scoring: UG_raw for a language = (cases passed) / (cases attempted-and-scored), pooled over the 3 trials, i.e. passed_cases / (12 * scored_trials). A trial whose program fails to build or fails to run scores 0 of 12 for that trial; it is not excluded, because failing to produce a runnable program is a failure to generalise. Normalisation family A.
tasks.reporting: Per-case pass rates per language are published, so a reader can see which category each language lost, rather than only the aggregate.
tasks.anti_hardcoding_check: The same mechanical check as PE-P1-svm-specA, with the same exemption set and the same single procedure (hit => COMPLIANCE_FAIL, no human review), applied against this task's own golden file and its own task_spec.md.
tasks.inlined_inputs_statement: Every one of the twelve cases now states its fixed inputs and, where the value is a direct consequence of those inputs and of the frozen generator, its expected value, inside this document. An independent analyst holding only this document can reproduce every UG number without access to task_spec.md, the golden file, or this conversation. task_spec.md carries the same inputs byte-identically for all ten languages. If the frozen golden file disagrees with an expected_value stated here, the discrepancy BLOCKS the run and is resolved before the first scored trial; it is never resolved after a trial has run and never by amending the value to match an observation.

tasks.name: Prompt Robustness
tasks.underlying_task: One fixed semantic task, identical in required behaviour across all three variations and all ten languages: generate 200,000 unit floats from the frozen LCG (seed 1); compute and print, one per line and in this order, the count as an integer, the arithmetic mean to 6 decimals, the population variance to 6 decimals, the minimum to 6 decimals, the maximum to 6 decimals, then the five largest values in descending order to 6 decimals on one line separated by single spaces, then the number of values strictly greater than 0.5 as an integer.
tasks.normative_contract_block: All three variations embed a BYTE-IDENTICAL normative block that states the LCG formula, the seed, the sample count, the exact output lines, their order, and the 6-decimal formatting rule. Only the material surrounding that block differs. This guarantees that the requested behaviour is unchanged across variations, which is the requirement of spec 22, and that a variation cannot accidentally change the task.

variations.description: Minimal imperative wording. The normative block is preceded by a single sentence naming the deliverable and followed by nothing. Bulleted, no prose rationale. Shortest of the three.

The same task described in full paragraphs with context and restatement, roughly 3x the length of v1. Output requirements are discussed in prose BEFORE the data-generation requirement is discussed, reversing v1's order, and the normative block appears at the END.
variations.ordering: prose context, prose statement of outputs, prose statement of data generation, normative block.

variations.description: The same task presented as a requirements table with numbered rows and a short field-schema table, with the normative block placed in the MIDDLE, between the requirements table and a closing acceptance-criteria table. Length between v1 and v2.
variations.ordering: requirements table, normative block, acceptance-criteria table.

variation_construction_rules: The same three variations are used for every one of the ten languages. Not one word of a variation differs by language except through the standard placeholder substitutions.

No variation adds, removes, weakens, or strengthens any behavioural requirement. This is verified mechanically before the run by diffing each variation against the normative block and confirming the block is present byte-identically and that no sentence outside it contains a numeral, a format specifier, or an output-line description that contradicts it. The verification output is preserved at tasks/PR-R1/variation_equivalence_check.txt.
No variation mentions any language, any API, or any syntax.
The variations were written before any trial and are frozen.
tasks.oracle: Mechanical field comparison exactly as in PE-P1: integer fields exact, float fields within absolute 1e-06 / relative 1e-09 against the frozen golden file. Identical oracle for all three variations.

metric_definition.per_variation_rate: p_v(L) = (trials of variation v in language L whose INITIAL generation passed the oracle) / (scored trials of variation v in language L). Initial generation only, no repairs, because robustness is about the prompt's effect on the first response.
metric_definition.score_raw: PromptRobustness_raw(L) = min over v in {v1, v2, v3} of p_v(L).
metric_definition.why_min_and_not_spread: A spread-based measure (max - min) would award 100 to a language that fails under every phrasing, which is the opposite of what spec 22 asks. The worst-case correctness across equivalent phrasings answers 'does correctness remain stable' without rewarding uniform failure: a language correct under all three phrasings scores high, a language correct only under one scores low, a language correct under none scores 0. This choice was made and written down before any trial and must not be changed afterwards.
mandatory_published_raw: max minus min over v (the stability spread)
metric_definition.precision: Each p_v comes from 5 trials and therefore has a resolution of 20 percentage points. The published table must carry that statement.

tasks.anti_hardcoding_check: The same mechanical check as PE-P1-svm-specA, with the same exemption set and the same single procedure (hit => COMPLIANCE_FAIL, no human review), applied against this task's own golden file and its own task_spec.md.

silent_bug_definition_and_measurement.definition: A generated program version is a SILENT BUG if and only if all of the following hold: (a) the build/parse step succeeded, or the language's frozen recipe has no separate build step; (b) the program ran to normal completion within the run timeout; (c) the process exit status is 0; (d) no line of its stderr matches that language's frozen runtime-error signature list; and (e) the oracle comparison FAILED. In words: it compiled, it ran, it said nothing was wrong, and the answer was wrong.
explicitly_not_a_silent_bug: a program that printed a specified error line the task asked for and was correct to print
a program that reported its own failure on stderr and exited non-zero
silent_bug_definition_and_measurement.classification_is_mechanical: No human judges whether a wrong answer was 'obviously wrong'. Conditions (a) to (e) are evaluated by scripts/classify_version.py from recorded exit codes, recorded stderr, and the oracle result.

runtime_error_signature_lists._purpose: Condition (d). A language must not be credited with a 'silent' failure when its runtime did in fact report a fault on stderr while still exiting 0 (possible in some runtimes).
runtime_error_signature_lists.matching_rule: Case-sensitive regular-expression search, anchored as written, applied line by line to the captured stderr. The lists were written from each toolchain's documented fault output before any trial and are published; a fault text observed during the run that is not on a list is added ONLY by amending this document before any score is computed, and any such amendment is recorded in _deviations.json with its date and reason. After the first score is computed the lists are closed.
runtime_error_signature_lists.validation_required: Every list in this block is subject to syntax_hallucination_resistance_definition.signature_list_validation, including its blocking condition. An unvalidated runtime-error list would misclassify OUTPUT_MISMATCH as SILENT_BUG (or the reverse) for that language on a 12 percent metric.

primary_metric.name: Silent Bug Resistance
primary_metric.raw: SilentBugRate(L) = silent_bug_versions(L) / incorrect_versions(L), where incorrect_versions is every generated version in every scored trial of language L (initial plus each repair turn) whose classification is not PASS, and silent_bug_versions is the subset of those meeting conditions (a)-(e).
primary_metric.why_this_denominator: The denominator is 'versions that were wrong', not 'versions that ran' and not 'all versions'. Dividing by all versions would reward a language for failing to compile, because a program that never builds can never be a silent bug. Dividing by versions that ran would shrink the denominator of exactly those languages whose compiler catches errors early, which penalises early detection. Asking instead 'when this language's generated code was wrong, how often was it wrong silently' is what spec 17 and 18 are about: whether an invalid value is silently transformed into an apparently valid one and execution continues. Compile failures and crashes are loud failures and correctly sit in the denominator.
primary_metric.zero_denominator: If a language produced no incorrect version at all, SilentBugRate is 0 and the score is 100, recorded with n_incorrect = 0 and the note that no incorrect version existed to fail silently.
primary_metric.low_precision_flag: Any language whose incorrect_versions count is below 10 is flagged 'low precision (n=<count>)' in the published table, and its Silent Bug Resistance value must not be used to claim a ranking difference of a few points.
mandatory_published_raw: versions_that_reached_execution per language (build succeeded or not applicable, AND the process actually ran)
the secondary figure silent_bug_versions / total_versions, published beside the primary rate
the THIRD framing silent_bug_versions / versions_that_reached_execution, published beside the primary rate; this is the framing free of the compile-failure dilution

the Pearson correlation across the ten languages between compile-failure rate and Silent Bug Resistance score, with the ten (x, y) pairs printed so a reader can see the relationship rather than take the coefficient on trust
a per-language row stating whether that language's FROZEN RELEASE RECIPE leaves integer arithmetic overflow CHECKED, WRAPPING, or UNDEFINED (see arithmetic_configuration_disclosure)
the list of every silent-bug version's trial path
primary_metric.denominator_dilution_disclosure: The predeclared primary denominator, incorrect_versions, includes NO_ARTIFACT and COMPILE_FAIL versions. A version that never compiled can never be a silent bug, so every compile failure ENLARGES the denominator without being able to enter the numerator, which lowers the rate and RAISES the score. On the joint-heaviest metric in the table that is partly a reward for failing to compile, and the language that will compile-fail most is the one the model has least prior exposure to. The document's earlier rationale addressed only the opposite error (dividing by all versions), and the secondary framing silent/total shares the same defect because total also grows with compile failures. The raw is NOT changed post-freeze; the third framing below is the one free of the dilution and is published beside it.
primary_metric.frozen_disclosure_sentence: This metric's denominator includes versions that never ran; a language with more compile failures is diluted upward. Read the third framing, silent bugs per version that reached execution, beside it.

silent_bug_definition_and_measurement.preservation: Every silent-bug version is preserved in full in its versions/<version>/ directory with classification.json carrying "classification": "SILENT_BUG" and the five condition flags, and is listed in llm-practical/raw/silent_bugs.json with its trial path, task, language, version id, and the failing oracle fields. Spec 23 requires this and spec 32 forbids classifying a Silent Bug as a success.
silent_bug_definition_and_measurement.relationship_to_the_adversarial_suite: This metric measures silent bugs in LLM-GENERATED programs. The separate adversarial/safety suite of spec 17 and 18 measures each language's behaviour on the fixed defect set with benchmark-authored programs and produces the Early Error Detection stage scores of normalisation family F. The two are different evidence and are not merged; neither is used to adjust the other.

arithmetic_configuration_disclosure._why: Silent Bug Resistance measures whether a wrong value is delivered with no signal. Whether an arithmetic fault produces a signal is decided, for several of the ten, by the FROZEN RELEASE BUILD FLAGS rather than by the language core. Spec 7 requires release/optimised builds and the recipes are not changed; but the comparison must be labelled for what it is.

per_language.Quidra: CHECKED. quidra build keeps integer arithmetic overflow-checked (00_cross_language_constraints C-1: wraparound is not expressible; overflow raises runtime error[INTEGER_OVERFLOW]).
per_language.Swift: CHECKED. swiftc -O still traps on signed integer overflow.
per_language.Rust: WRAPPING. rustc -O leaves debug overflow checks off, so integer overflow wraps silently.
per_language.Zig: UNCHECKED. zig build-exe -OReleaseFast disables safety checks; integer overflow is illegal behaviour rather than a panic. -OReleaseSafe would trap.
per_language.C++: UNDEFINED. clang++ -O2 leaves signed integer overflow undefined; unsigned wraps.
per_language.Go: WRAPPING. Integer overflow wraps by language definition, independently of build flags.
per_language.Java: WRAPPING. Two's-complement wrap by language definition.
per_language.Kotlin: WRAPPING. Two's-complement wrap on the JVM by language definition.
per_language.Python: NOT APPLICABLE in the same sense. Integers are arbitrary precision; there is no integer overflow to signal.
per_language.TypeScript: NOT APPLICABLE in the same sense. Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles; exact integer range is lost silently beyond 2^53 rather than overflowing.

arithmetic_configuration_disclosure.frozen_disclosure_sentence: Silent Bug Resistance compares languages as configured by their frozen release recipes, not language cores. Four of the ten have integer arithmetic checks disabled or undefined by their release flags, two have wrapping fixed by their language definition, two have no comparable integer overflow at all, and two (Quidra and Swift) keep the check on. A silent wrong answer is more available to the first group as a consequence of that configuration.
arithmetic_configuration_disclosure.direction_of_the_effect: The disclosure runs in Quidra's favour on this metric and is published anyway: it tells the reader that part of any Quidra advantage here is a build-flag property shared with Swift, not a unique language property.
arithmetic_configuration_disclosure.optional_non_scoring_diagnostic: The final passing PE-P1 versions may additionally be rebuilt with `zig build-exe -OReleaseSafe` and `rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on` and re-run, and the resulting classifications published as a CLEARLY LABELLED NON-SCORING diagnostic. It never enters any score and never replaces the frozen-recipe figure.

syntax_hallucination_resistance_definiti.definition: A hallucination event is a generated version that refers to language surface that does not exist: either a named construct the language does not have (class H1) or a grammatical form the language does not accept (class H2).

classes.H1_nonexistent_named_construct: The version references an identifier, member, method, field, type, module, package, attribute, or macro that does not exist in the language or its standard library, detected by a toolchain diagnostic matching that language's H1 signature list, or by a runtime fault matching that language's H1 runtime signature list.
classes.H2_nonexistent_grammar: The version is rejected by the language's parser, detected by a toolchain diagnostic matching that language's H2 signature list. A parse rejection is treated as invented syntax.

syntax_hallucination_resistance_definiti.measurement_population: All INITIAL generations of every scored trial, pooled across every task, for that language. This is a large, identically constructed sample per language (28 initial generations per language under the frozen allocation: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1) and costs no extra trials. Repair versions are excluded from the primary figure because a repair turn has already been shown the diagnostic; their hallucination counts are published separately as a secondary figure.
syntax_hallucination_resistance_definiti.raw: HallucinationRate(L) = versions_with_at_least_one_H1_or_H2_event(L) / scored_initial_generations(L). Counted per version, not per diagnostic, so a language whose compiler emits many diagnostics for one mistake is not penalised for its diagnostic verbosity.

Zig: root source file struct .* has no member
no field or member function named

Java: class, interface, enum, or record expected
reached end of file while parsing

detection_coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.statement: Detection channels are the union of (a) build/parse diagnostics from the frozen recipe and (b) runtime fault output over the frozen inputs. The same two channels are applied to all ten languages. Their COVERAGE nevertheless differs: a statically checked language surfaces an H1 event in unreached code at build time, while Python surfaces it only if the code runs.
detection_coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.mitigation_applied: Every task's output contract requires that every computation the task specifies actually be executed and printed, so the frozen inputs drive the whole required program. This is why the contract mandates printing every field rather than a single summary value: it gives the dynamically checked languages execution coverage of the required code paths.
detection_coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.residual_limitation_recorded: Coverage of code paths the model wrote but that the task does not require to execute (a defensive branch, an unused helper) remains lower for Python and, where a type is erased at runtime, for TypeScript executed through node. The residual is stated in the published results next to this metric. It is NOT corrected by a per-language adjustment factor, because inventing one would be a post-hoc transformation, and it is not hidden.
detection_coverage_asymmetry_disclosure.why_not_a_third_channel: A static symbol-existence auditor would have to be written per language, would have different fidelity in each, and would itself become an uncontrolled source of cross-language difference. Two channels applied identically, with the residual disclosed, is the honest option.

mandatory_published_raw: per language: scored_initial_generations, versions_with_H1, versions_with_H2, versions_with_either, the rate
the verbatim first matching diagnostic line for every counted version, with its trial path
the same figures for repair versions, published separately
syntax_hallucination_resistance_definiti.H1_symmetry_note: 'no matching function for call to' was removed from the C++ list and 'is not a type' from the Go list. Both fire on ordinary overload and type errors against symbols that DO exist, i.e. they count non-hallucinations as hallucinations, and no other language's list carried an analogous over-broad pattern. Removing them makes the ten lists symmetric in what class of fault they detect: a reference to a name that does not exist. Overload and arity mismatches are real faults and are still fully visible: they produce COMPILE_FAIL, which is scored by Compile/Parse Success Rate and Correct@1. They are simply not counted as INVENTED SURFACE, because they are not. No pattern was added to any language's list to compensate; adding a compensating over-broad pattern to the other nine would have been the symmetric error rather than a fix.
syntax_hallucination_resistance_definiti.class_boundary: H1 is 'the name does not exist'. H2 is 'the grammar does not accept this'. Neither class covers 'the name exists but the call does not type-check'. That third class is deliberately outside this metric for all ten languages alike, and is scored where it belongs, in compile success and correctness.

signature_list_validation._authority: spec 10.4 mandatory pre-flight validation, item 3: every validator must be shown to both pass and fail.
signature_list_validation._why: These lists drive Syntax Hallucination Resistance (7 percent) and the SILENT_BUG / OUTPUT_MISMATCH split that feeds Silent Bug Resistance (12 percent). A list that never matches its own toolchain's real fault text records zero events and scores 100 by INSTRUMENT FAILURE rather than by the language behaving well. That failure mode is most likely for whichever toolchain's diagnostic wording was least verified, and the lists were asserted to have been written from documented fault output with no evidence preserved.
signature_list_validation.procedure: For EACH of the ten languages and EACH of its three lists (H1, H2, runtime-error signatures), the benchmark authors author two fixtures: (i) a POSITIVE fixture, a small program that provokes exactly that class of fault under the frozen recipe, and (ii) a NEGATIVE fixture, a small correct program that must produce no match on that list. Both are built and run under the frozen recipe on this host.
signature_list_validation.recorded: The verbatim diagnostic text of every positive fixture, the list entry that matched it, and the no-match result of every negative fixture are preserved at llm-practical/config/signature_validation/<language>.json, hashed, before the first scored trial.
signature_list_validation.blocking_condition: A list with NO demonstrated positive match, or with a positive match on its negative fixture, BLOCKS the run until the real diagnostic text is recorded and the list corrected. This is the only circumstance in which a signature list may be amended, it is the amendment path already allowed by amendment_and_freeze_rules, and every amendment is entered in _deviations.json with class 'signature_list_amendment', its date, the added or removed pattern, the verbatim observed fault text, and the reason.
signature_list_validation.applies_to_all_ten_equally: No language's list is exempt, and a list is not accepted because its wording looks plausible. Quidra's list is validated against Quidra 0.2.0's real output exactly as C++'s is validated against clang's.

version_classification_ladder._purpose: One mechanical classifier turns a generated version into exactly one class. Every metric is computed from these classes plus recorded counts. scripts/classify_version.py implements it and is identical for all ten languages.

classes_in_ladder_order_worst_to_best.condition: The subagent returned without a file at generated/<ENTRY_FILENAME>, or the file is empty, or more than one source file was created when the task required one.
The build command exited non-zero, timed out, or produced no runnable artefact. For a language with no separate build step, a parse failure detected by running the program with no work performed.
The build succeeded but the run exited non-zero, was killed by a signal, or hit the run timeout.
Conditions (a)-(e) of the silent-bug definition all hold. A wrong answer delivered with no signal of any kind.

The run completed with exit 0 and the oracle failed, but stderr carried a matching runtime-error signature, so the program did signal that something was wrong. Ranked above SILENT_BUG because the failure was at least observable.
The oracle output matched but a mechanical compliance item failed, including the anti-hard-coding check. Not a PASS.
The build succeeded (or is not applicable), the run exited 0 within the timeout, every oracle field matched, and every compliance item passed.

version_classification_ladder.exactly_one_class: Evaluated in the order NO_ARTIFACT, COMPILE_FAIL, RUNTIME_FAIL, then (oracle pass and compliance pass) PASS, then COMPLIANCE_FAIL, then SILENT_BUG vs OUTPUT_MISMATCH by the stderr signature test. The first condition that holds is the class.
version_classification_ladder.improvement_ladder_for_diagnosis: A repair turn IMPROVED if rank(new) > rank(old), or rank(new) == rank(old) and checks_passed(new) > checks_passed(old). Otherwise it did not improve and is counted as a misdiagnosis. This is mechanical and uses no human judgement about whether the model's stated reasoning was right.

metric_definitions_and_weights._authority: spec 9.1. The weights below are the complete spec 9.1 table, copied without alteration.
metric_definitions_and_weights.weights_frozen_statement: These eighteen weights are FROZEN. They must not be altered after any scored LLM output has been observed (spec 9.1, spec 32). They sum to 100 percent. No weight may be added, removed, reallocated, or renormalised except by the N/A policy of spec 26 applied to a genuinely inapplicable metric, and every such renormalisation must be published with its reason.

metrics.definition: scored trials whose INITIAL generation produced a usable artefact (class is not NO_ARTIFACT) / scored trials. Provider and infrastructure failures are excluded from both numerator and denominator and recorded separately.
metrics.aggregation: unweighted mean over the applicable task set (spec 25.2)

metrics.definition: initial generations whose class rank is >= 2 (i.e. not NO_ARTIFACT and not COMPILE_FAIL) / initial generations with an artefact. For a language whose frozen recipe has no separate build step, the parse check is the only build-stage check and is applied in the same slot; this difference is a property of the language's toolchain and is recorded, not adjusted.

SCORED value: initial generations classified PASS / scored initial generations on PE-P1-svm-specA ALONE, the five-trial primary implementation cell that spec 6.2 names as the source of Correct@1. The scored value is not an average over tasks.
metrics.aggregation: none: single task (PE-P1-svm-specA). The previous rule ('computed per task, then averaged over tasks') diluted the one cell whose five trials spec 6.2 specifically mandated for this metric to one tenth of a 12 percent weight, with the other nine tenths coming from cells whose resolution this document itself states as 100 and 33 percentage points. Averaging cannot manufacture precision the measurement does not have; it only moves a score through aggregation rather than measurement.
metrics.non_scoring_companion_table: Per-task initial-generation pass rates for PE-P2 through PE-P6, UG-G1 and the three PR variations are still computed, still published, and clearly labelled NON-SCORING, each carrying its own trial count and precision sentence. Nothing is hidden; it simply does not enter the 12 percent.

metrics.definition: FROZEN INTERPRETATION: pass@N over N independent INITIAL generations, no repairs. For a cell with N trials, the cell contributes 1 if at least one of its N initial generations classified PASS, else 0. Computed ONLY over cells with N >= 5, which are PE-P1-svm-specA and the three PR variations. Cells with N = 1 are excluded because there Correct@N is identical to Correct@1 and would double-count it; the exclusion is published.
metrics.aggregation: unweighted mean over the four eligible tasks

metrics.definition: For each scored trial's FINAL version: oracle checks passed / oracle checks total, where the check set is the task's fixed oracle_schema field list. Averaged over trials, then over tasks. A version with no artefact or a failed build scores 0 of its task's checks.
trials whose initial generation was not PASS and whose final version (within the 3-repair budget) is PASS / trials whose initial generation was not PASS.
metrics.zero_denominator: If a language had no failing initial generation on any scored task, this metric is N/A for that language with reason 'no_failing_initial_generation', excluded from the applicable-weight denominator, and the remaining weights renormalised per spec 26. This is a genuine inapplicability, not a missing capability, and it is published.
metrics.aggregation: pooled over all scored trials of all tasks, because the denominator is small; the per-task breakdown is published

metrics.definition: Per spec 25.1 family E: per trial, 100 * (1 - repair_turns_used / 3), clipped to [0, 100]. A Correct@1 trial used 0 repair turns and scores 100. A trial still not PASS after repair_03 used 3 turns and scores 0 and is also a repair failure. Trial-level scores are averaged.
metrics.aggregation: mean over all scored trials, then unweighted mean over tasks

metrics.definition: Per trial that used at least one repair turn: improving_repair_turns / repair_turns_used, using the mechanical improvement ladder. A trial that used no repair turn scores 1.0 (nothing was misdiagnosed). Averaged over trials. Also recorded per spec 19: diagnosis turns, repair turns, tokens to first improving repair, and misdiagnosis count, all preserved per trial.
metrics.no_invented_human_times: Spec 19 forbids inventing human debugging times. No human participant study was performed, so no human minutes are claimed anywhere. Agent wall-clock per turn IS measured and recorded, alongside turns and tokens.
metrics.aggregation: mean over trials, then unweighted mean over tasks

metrics.definition: See silent_bug_definition_and_measurement. Raw = silent_bug_versions / incorrect_versions, pooled over all generated versions of all scored trials.
See syntax_hallucination_resistance_definition. Raw = versions_with_H1_or_H2 / scored_initial_generations, pooled over all tasks.

For each scored trial's FINAL version: compliance checklist items satisfied / checklist items, from scripts/check_compliance.py. Averaged over trials, then over tasks. The checklist is fixed per task before any trial and is identical in content for all ten languages.
min over the three variations of the per-variation initial-generation pass rate. See the PR task entry.
metrics.aggregation: single task set; no cross-task mean

metrics.definition: passed cases / (12 * scored trials) on UG-G1-unseen. See the UG task entry.
metrics.aggregation: single task; per-case and per-category breakdown published

metrics.definition: Raw value per language per task = the lexical source-token count of the FINAL PASSING version, by the frozen counter in source_token_counting. Lower is better. Per task, Score_i = 100 * best_positive_raw / raw_i over the languages that have a passing version on that task; the language's metric score is the UNWEIGHTED MEAN over the FIXED applicable_workload_set above, which is the same six tasks for every language.
metrics.no_passing_version: A task in the applicable_workload_set for which a language has no passing version contributes a PER-TASK SCORE OF 0 for that language. It is NOT omitted from that language's mean. The previous rule ('the mean over the tasks where it does have one') made the averaged task set differ per language and conditioned the score on success: failing the task on which a language would have been most verbose RAISED its score. It also contradicted this metric's own sibling rule that a language with no passing version anywhere scores 0 rather than N/A, and Generated Code Performance's identical rule. A language with no passing version on any of the six therefore scores 0, which now falls out of the per-task rule rather than needing a special case. This is predeclared and applies identically to all ten languages.
metrics.family_C_disclosure: Where the applicable raw values on a task span a factor of 100 or more, spec 25.1 requires publishing the raw value in its natural unit for every language, the ratio raw_i / best_positive_raw, and the note that the ratios rather than the compressed scores carry the comparison between non-leading languages. That publication is mandatory here.

metrics.definition: Raw value per language per task = the mean over scored trials of that trial's cumulative harness-reported OUTPUT tokens (initial generation plus every repair turn). Lower is better. Score_i = 100 * best_positive_raw / raw_i.
metrics.availability_condition: This metric depends on the harness reporting per-subagent token usage. If usage is reported for a trial, it is recorded in tokens/usage.json and used. If usage is NOT reported for ANY trial of ANY language, the metric is marked N/A for ALL ten languages with reason 'harness_does_not_expose_token_usage', its 3 percent is removed from the applicable-weight denominator, the remaining seventeen weights are renormalised per spec 26, and the removal is published prominently. If usage is reported for some languages and not others, the metric is marked N/A for all ten anyway, because a partial measurement would not be comparable; the partial data is still published as a non-scoring diagnostic.
metrics.no_proxy_in_scoring: No character-count or word-count proxy is ever substituted for reported token usage in the score. A proxy figure (output bytes of the model's messages) may be published clearly labelled as a non-scoring diagnostic, and must never appear in a scored column.

metrics.definition: Wall-clock execution time of the FINAL PASSING version on PE-P1-svm-specA, measured with the frozen measurement harness under the same conditions as every other timing measurement in this run: 3 discarded warm-up runs then 7 measured runs, median as the representative raw value, all runs and the dispersion preserved (spec 12, spec 25.2).
metrics.managed_runtime_handling: Each of the 3 warm-up and 7 measured runs is a FRESH PROCESS started by the frozen run command. The scored raw value therefore INCLUDES runtime startup and JIT warm-up for Java, Kotlin, TypeScript/node and Python, and includes process start for the compiled languages. That is the scored figure for all ten, stated here rather than left implicit. A separate IN-PROCESS steady-state figure is measured for the four managed runtimes by the frozen in-process protocol (the frozen run command is invoked once and the workload body is executed 10 times inside that process; the median of the last 7 is the steady-state raw value; the same protocol is also run for the six compiled languages so the diagnostic exists for all ten and is not a special accommodation). The steady-state figure is published as a NON-SCORING diagnostic beside the scored figure and never enters any score, so spec 12's requirement that cold-start and steady-state are never mixed is checkable rather than unfalsifiable.
metrics.quidra_mode: SELECTION, NOT COMBINATION. Spec 11 asks for a rule combining Quidra's native and interpreter evidence; this document instead SELECTS one mode. The Quidra column uses NATIVE mode, matching the release-build treatment of every other compiled language, and the interpreter-mode number for the same generated program is measured and published as a separate raw row (spec 11, spec 29) without entering the column. Native is the faster of the two, so this is the most Quidra-favourable of the available selections for this metric and for Generated Code Memory Efficiency. The symmetry argument for it is real and it was predeclared before any result, which is what spec 11 requires on timing; what was missing was any way for a reader to see what the selection is worth. Obligation O15 supplies that.
metrics.no_passing_version: Score 0, not N/A, with reason 'no_passing_generated_program'. Predeclared, identical for all ten languages. This is a real outcome of the thing being measured: the metric asks how fast the code the model produced runs, and producing no correct runnable code is the worst possible answer to that question, not an inapplicable one.
metrics.workload_set_is_language_independent: The applicable workload set is exactly {PE-P1-svm-specA} for every one of the ten languages. A language with no passing version there scores 0, with reason 'no_passing_generated_program'. The earlier text said both 'Measured on PE-P1-svm-specA' and 'where a language has more than one passing task, the unweighted mean of the per-task family-C scores is used', which are two different aggregations in one sentence and the second made the averaged task set depend on which tasks a language happened to pass. Spec 25.2 requires normalisation at the lowest comparable workload level over a FIXED applicable workload set; a set that varies by language is not comparable.

metrics.definition: Peak resident set size of the FINAL PASSING version over the measured runs, median, by the same frozen measurement harness. Same warm-up, same run count, same dispersion preservation, same managed-runtime separation, same Quidra native-mode rule, same no-passing-version rule (score 0 with reason).
metrics.workload_set_is_language_independent: The applicable workload set is exactly {PE-P1-svm-specA} for every one of the ten languages. A language with no passing version there scores 0, with reason 'no_passing_generated_program'. The earlier text said both 'Measured on PE-P1-svm-specA' and 'where a language has more than one passing task, the unweighted mean of the per-task family-C scores is used', which are two different aggregations in one sentence and the second made the averaged task set depend on which tasks a language happened to pass. Spec 25.2 requires normalisation at the lowest comparable workload level over a FIXED applicable workload set; a set that varies by language is not comparable.

metrics.definition: Wall-clock time of the frozen build command on the FINAL PASSING version, median of 7 measured builds from a clean build directory. For a language whose frozen recipe has no separate build step, this metric is N/A for that language with reason 'language_has_no_separate_build_step_in_its_frozen_recipe', excluded from the applicable-weight denominator for that language only, and the remaining weights renormalised per spec 26. That is a genuine inapplicability of the quantity, not a missing capability being hidden: the language's startup and parse cost is still fully visible in Generated Code Performance, which measures the whole run. Same no-passing-version rule (score 0 with reason) for languages that do have a build step.
metrics.workload_set_is_language_independent: The applicable workload set is exactly {PE-P1-svm-specA} for every one of the ten languages. A language with no passing version there scores 0, with reason 'no_passing_generated_program'. The earlier text said both 'Measured on PE-P1-svm-specA' and 'where a language has more than one passing task, the unweighted mean of the per-task family-C scores is used', which are two different aggregations in one sentence and the second made the averaged task set depend on which tasks a language happened to pass. Spec 25.2 requires normalisation at the lowest comparable workload level over a FIXED applicable workload set; a set that varies by language is not comparable.

presentation_row_mapping._authority: spec 9.1, fixed so that two runs do not invent different correspondences.

metric_definitions_and_weights.presentation_is_presentation_only: The twelve-row table of spec 28.2 is presentation only. It displays twelve of the eighteen weighted metrics. The six listed above still carry their weights and still enter the LLM Practical Effectiveness Score. The full eighteen-metric breakdown is preserved in results/llm_practical_full_breakdown.{json,md} and the score is computed from the eighteen, never from the twelve.
metric_definitions_and_weights.score_formula: LLM Practical Effectiveness Score(L) = sum over applicable metrics m of ( weight_m * Score_m(L) ) / sum over applicable metrics m of weight_m. Scores clipped to [0, 100], reported to two decimal places, ranked on unrounded values (spec 25.3).
metric_definitions_and_weights.ranking: An independent LLM Practical Effectiveness Ranking is produced from this score alone. It is never merged with Intrinsic Learnability, Semantic Compression, or Standard, and no cross-evaluation overall score or overall ranking is created (spec 28.2, spec 32).

na_policy_for_llm_practical.rule: N/A is never silently converted to zero and never used to let a missing capability escape scoring. A genuinely inapplicable metric is excluded from that language's applicable-weight denominator and the remaining weights are renormalised.

the_only_permitted_na_reasons.scope: all ten languages simultaneously or none
the_only_permitted_na_reasons.justification: The quantity is not observable through this client. It is not a property of any language.
There is no build command to time. The cost is not hidden: it is inside Generated Code Performance, which times the whole run.
There was nothing to repair. Repair Efficiency still scores 100 for such a language by family E, so the language is not credited twice.

the_only_permitted_na_reasons.metric: any metric whose cells all failed after 3 retries on a CASE (a) infrastructure event
the_only_permitted_na_reasons.justification: Spec 6.2 forbids converting provider/infrastructure failure into a language or model failure. This reason code is reachable ONLY through case (a) of retry_policy_infrastructure.agent_self_exhaustion_split (a provider or transport stall) and the provider/transport/host classes. A case (b) agent-budget exhaustion is scored, never retried, and can never produce this N/A. The shortfall is published in _deviations.json and in the results summary.

explicitly_not_na: A language that produced no passing program scores 0 on Generated Code Performance, Generated Code Memory Efficiency, Generated Code Compile Performance (if it has a build step) and Source Token Efficiency, with the reason recorded. It is not N/A.
A language the model handles badly is scored badly, not marked N/A.
A capability a language lacks that a task requires produces a failing class for that task, not N/A.

A task in a family-C metric's fixed applicable workload set on which a language has no passing version contributes a per-task score of 0, not an omission from that language's mean. Omitting it would let a language be scored only on the tasks it succeeded at.
A trial in which the model exhausted its wall-clock or context budget while actively working is classified from the artefact on disk and scored. It is not N/A and it is not infrastructure.
A facility prohibited on PE-P5/PE-P6 that a language happens to ship built in does not make the task N/A for that language; the language implements the engine like the other nine.
na_policy_for_llm_practical.every_na_documented: Every N/A written anywhere in the LLM Practical results carries its reason_code, the affected language, the affected metric, the renormalised applicable-weight denominator, and the resulting score both with and without the exclusion, so the effect of the exclusion is visible.

source_token_counting._purpose: Source Token Efficiency needs one counter applied identically to ten languages.
source_token_counting.governing_implementation: The Semantic Compression track's frozen source tokenizer (scripts/tokenize_probe.py) governs BOTH tracks; this section states the behaviour it must have, and where the two disagree the implementation as corrected by CORRECTIONS.md D-4 wins and this section is the defect. Exactly one implementation is used for all ten languages and its SHA-256 is recorded in the results and in frozen_input_digests.
source_token_counting.rule: Read the source file as UTF-8. Remove comments using the language's comment syntax as listed in the tokenizer's fixed per-language comment table (line-comment prefix and block-comment delimiters only; no other language knowledge is used). Then emit tokens by scanning left to right and matching, in this order: (1) a string or character literal, DECOMPOSED as in methodology 02 section 4.4(a) as corrected in CORRECTIONS.md D-4 - the literal shell counts as ONE token regardless of its length, and each interpolation hole pays ONE TOKEN PER DELIMITER ACTUALLY WRITTEN (a braced or parenthesised form such as {c}, ${c} or \(c) costs two: HOLE_OPEN + HOLE_CLOSE; a bare sigil form such as $c costs one: HOLE), PLUS the tokens of the embedded expression, counted by these same rules; (2) a numeric literal; (3) an identifier or keyword, matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* plus any non-ASCII letter; (4) a maximal run of operator or punctuation characters that the language's fixed operator table lists as a single operator, otherwise a single character. Whitespace and newlines are not tokens.
source_token_counting.why_a_lexical_counter_and_not_the_model_: The model's own tokenizer is not exposed by this client for arbitrary strings, and a BPE count would make Source Token Efficiency partly a measure of how the tokenizer happens to segment each language's identifiers. The lexical counter measures source structure, is reproducible by a third party with no provider access, and is applied identically to all ten. Where the harness does report input-token counts for packs, those are published beside the lexical counts and never substituted for them.
source_token_counting.comment_handling_disclosure: Comments are removed before counting, for all ten languages identically. This means a language whose generated code carries more explanatory comments is not penalised, and one that carries fewer is not rewarded. The comment-inclusive count is also published as a raw figure.
source_token_counting.interpolation_rule_provenance: The earlier wording here ('a string or character literal including its delimiters, counted as ONE token regardless of length', with no mention of interpolation) read literally as a flat one-token-per-hole exemption. CORRECTIONS.md D-4 identified exactly that exemption as QUIDRA BIAS and removed it from the Semantic Compression track: it granted a flat discount to Python, TypeScript, Kotlin, Swift and Quidra, and nothing to C++, Go, Java, Rust and Zig, which must spell out a call form and pay every '(', ',' and ')'. None of this document's conformance vectors exercised interpolation, so the vectors could not detect the discrepancy, and an independent analyst implementing Source Token Efficiency from this document alone would have reproduced the removed bias. The rule above is now the D-4-corrected rule verbatim, so the two tracks count the same way. Direction of the correction: it RAISES Quidra's token count and therefore LOWERS Quidra's Source Token Efficiency.

trial_preservation_layout._authority: spec 23 (complete preservation of LLM trials) and spec 24 (prompt preservation).
trial_preservation_layout.reconstruction_guarantee: From this layout alone, with no access to this conversation and no access to the model, a third party can reconstruct prompt -> generated program -> failure -> diagnosis -> repair -> final result for every trial, including every version that contained a Silent Bug.
trial_preservation_layout.path_grammar: <root>/<task_id>/<language_slug>/trial_<NN>/ where NN is the trial index zero-padded to two digits, 01-based. task_id is one of the frozen ids in trial_allocation. language_slug is one of quidra, python, cpp, rust, go, java, typescript, kotlin, swift, zig. Nothing else appears at those levels.
directory_tree: <root>/_aborted/<task_id>__<language_slug>__trial_<NN>__attempt_<A>/   (preserved partial directory of any attempt discarded for an infrastructure event)
trial_preservation_layout.version_directories_are_created_only_whe: repair_02/ exists only if repair turn 2 was issued. Its absence means the trial ended earlier and is not a gap in the record; manifest.json states repair_turns_used explicitly.

manifest.json.note: 'scored' is false for the DIAG-NOPACK trials and for any invalidated trial; 'excluded_reason' says why.

file_semantics.prompts/system_prompt.txt: The fully substituted system prompt, byte-exact as delivered.
file_semantics.prompts/user_prompt_initial.txt: The fully substituted task prompt, byte-exact as delivered, including the task specification text and the on-disk pointers to the pack.
file_semantics.prompts/pack_manifest.json: Relative path, byte size, and SHA-256 of every file under prompts/pack/, plus the pack token counts by the frozen counter.
file_semantics.prompts/pack/: A verbatim copy of every file the trial could read as reference material. Spec 24 requires supplied language specifications and examples to be preserved; keeping them inside the trial, rather than only by reference, means a third party needs nothing else.
file_semantics.prompts/repair_prompt_NN.txt: The fully substituted repair prompt, byte-exact as delivered, including the real truncated diagnostics.
file_semantics.prompts/final_input_reconstruction.json: An ordered list of every message delivered to the model in this trial, each as {role, source_file, sha256}, so the exact final input presented to the model can be reconstructed byte for byte (spec 24).
file_semantics.versions/<id>/model_output.md: The subagent's raw returned text for that turn, verbatim, before any extraction.
file_semantics.versions/<id>/source/<ENTRY_FILENAME>: The source file exactly as it stood on disk when the turn ended. Read-only (0444). This is the artefact that is built and scored.
file_semantics.versions/<id>/oracle_diff.txt: Expected vs actual for every failing check, verbatim and untruncated. The truncated form is what went into the repair prompt; this is the full record.

versions/<id>/classification.json.note: silent_bug_conditions records the five boolean conditions (a)-(e) individually, so the classification can be re-derived by hand.

file_semantics.versions/<id>/sha256sums.txt: SHA-256, byte size, and mtime in nanoseconds of every file under source/, captured before any build step. Re-verified at scoring; a mismatch invalidates the trial.

diagnosis/diagnosis_NN.json.note: 'improved' and 'misdiagnosis' are computed by the mechanical improvement ladder. source_diff_unified is a unified diff from the previous version's source to this one, so the repair itself is visible.

tokens/usage.json.note: per_turn carries {version_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, wall_clock_ns}. Any field the harness does not report is null, never estimated. 'source_of_numbers' records exactly which harness field each number came from, or 'unavailable'.

file_semantics.logs/agent_tool_calls.jsonl: One JSON object per tool call the subagent made: timestamp_utc, tool, arguments_summary, allowed_or_denied, duration_ns. This is the audit trail for the no-retrieval and no-human-edit enforcement.
file_semantics.logs/timeline.jsonl: Ordered events: trial_start, prompt_delivered, turn_end, build_start/end, run_start/end, oracle_start/end, repair_issued, trial_end, each with timestamp_utc.
file_semantics.logs/errors.txt: Any orchestrator-side error text for this trial, verbatim. Infrastructure events also appear in the run-level _infrastructure_events.jsonl.

final/result.json.note: measured_* are present only when the final version is PASS, because performance is measured on passing programs only; otherwise null with the reason 'no_passing_generated_program'.

file_semantics.final/source/<ENTRY_FILENAME>: A read-only copy of the final version's source, so the end state is reachable without walking the version chain.
file_semantics.scratch/: Everything the trial agent wrote under <trial>/scratch/, preserved verbatim and made read-only after the trial. It is NOT scored, is never built, and never enters an oracle; it is preserved because spec 23 requires that a third party be able to reconstruct the trial, and working files the agent produced are part of what happened. The system prompt now tells the model this directory exists and that nothing there is scored, so the affordance is real and identical for all ten languages rather than a permission the model was never told it had.

index_files._index.json: One row per trial with: task_id, language, trial_index, schedule_index, scored, final_classification, repair_turns_used, correct_at_1, path. Plus a header block with per-cell trials_planned, trials_executed, trials_scored. This is the file the reporting obligation on executed counts is computed from.
index_files._execution_order.json: The frozen schedule: the enumerated triples, their LCG sort keys, the deterministic spread-constraint repair steps, and the final ordered list. Written before the first trial.
index_files._infrastructure_events.jsonl: Every provider, rate-limit, transport, timeout, context-exhaustion, harness, host, and model-identity event, with the action taken. Separate from all language and model failures, per spec 6.2.
index_files._deviations.json: Every departure from this frozen configuration, with class, affected cells, reason, date, and effect on the metrics. Classes: source_mutated_after_capture, retrieval_violation, infrastructure_exhausted, trial_count_shortfall, signature_list_amendment, other. An empty list is written if there are none, so the absence of deviations is itself recorded rather than inferred.

trial_preservation_layout.immutability: Trial directories are written once and then made read-only. Re-running a cell writes a new attempt directory; it never overwrites a preserved one. Nothing under trials/ is deleted, including aborted attempts, failed generations, and silent-bug versions (spec 32 forbids hiding failed trials and inconvenient raw data).
trial_preservation_layout.prompt_preservation_cross_reference: Spec 24 additionally requires preservation of adversarial-test prompts, unseen-case prompts, and prompt-robustness variations. The unseen-case and robustness prompts live in these trial directories by construction (UG-G1-unseen and PR-R1-v1..v3 are task_ids). The authored source of every task specification and every prompt variation, before substitution, is preserved at llm-practical/tasks/<task_id>/ with SHA-256, and the adversarial-test prompts belong to the adversarial suite's own directory.

reporting_obligations._authority: spec 6.2 allocation paragraph, spec 25.1 family-C disclosure, spec 26, spec 32.
obligations: O1. Publish trials_planned, trials_executed, and trials_scored for every (task_id, language) cell. Never publish a planned count as though it were executed.

O2. Attach the frozen precision sentence to every table row backed by fewer than five trials per language, stating the actual N, AND to every row whose scored value can take fewer than ten distinct values, stating the attainable value set. Prompt Robustness and Correct@N are covered by the second clause even though both are backed by five-trial cells.

O2b. Any aggregated row whose per-task components have mixed trial counts must publish the per-task N vector and the effective resolution of the aggregate, and must not present the aggregate as carrying the precision of its best-measured component.
O3. Never describe a few-point difference between languages in a one-trial row as a resolved difference, and never attach a ranking, interval, or significance claim to it.
O4. Publish, for the five-trial cells, the per-trial outcomes and the statement that a five-trial rate resolves to 20 percentage points.
O5. Publish the duplication rate per cell where deterministic decoding produced byte-identical trials.
O6. Publish infrastructure events per language and state that none of them entered any metric.

O7. For every family-C metric whose applicable raw values span a factor of 100 or more, publish the raw value in its natural unit for every language, the ratio to the best value, and the compression note required by spec 25.1.
O8. Publish every N/A with its reason_code, its effect on the applicable-weight denominator, and the score with and without the exclusion.
O9. Publish the full eighteen-metric weighted breakdown alongside the twelve-row presentation table, and state that the score comes from the eighteen.
O10. Publish the silent-bug list, the hallucination-match list, and the detection-coverage asymmetry disclosure.
O11. Publish the statement that no generated source was edited by a human, with the count of trials whose source hashes verified.
O12. Publish the DIAG-NOPACK results in their own table, labelled a diagnostic of prior knowledge, with an explicit statement that they contribute to no score (spec 9).
O13. Publish _deviations.json contents in the results summary, including the case where it is empty.

O14. Publish, beside the LLM Practical Effectiveness table, a REFERENCE-COVERAGE column giving sections_included / sections_available and tokens_included / tokens_available for each of the ten languages, with the frozen sentence: 'The 20,000-token document-order budget gives Quidra approximately N percent of its language definition and the incumbent languages a prefix of M percent of theirs. This asymmetry is uncorrected and favours the language the model has least prior exposure to.' N and M are filled from the published counts in packs/pack_token_counts.json; M is reported per language, not only as a single figure.

O15. Publish Quidra's LLM Practical Effectiveness Score RECOMPUTED with the interpreter-mode values substituted for Generated Code Performance and Generated Code Memory Efficiency, beside the primary score, so the effect of the native-mode selection is visible rather than absorbed. Publish the same recomputation for any other language for which the run measures more than one execution mode, so the obligation is stated in terms any of the ten could trigger.

O16. Publish the three Silent Bug Resistance framings side by side (per incorrect version, per total version, per version that reached execution), the per-language compile-failure counts, the correlation pairs, and the arithmetic-configuration row required by silent_bug_definition_and_measurement.arithmetic_configuration_disclosure.

O17. Publish the per-language case (a) / case (b) split of agent self-exhaustion required by retry_policy_infrastructure.agent_self_exhaustion_split, and state that case (b) counts were scored and entered the metrics.

O18. Publish the signature-list validation results, the deny-list false-denial counts, the anti-hardcoding pre-flight results and the exact-match integer stability table, all of which must have passed before the run started.
O19. Publish frozen_input_digests in full in the results summary, and state that every digest was verified at scoring time and matched.
reporting_obligations.frozen_precision_sentence: This row is measured with N trial(s) per language. Differences of a few points between languages are not resolved by this measurement and must not be read as a ranking.

C3. Golden outputs generated from the pinned references and frozen, with SHA-256 and provenance recorded, AND common_task_contract.exact_match_integer_field_preflight passed for every task with an exact-match integer field.
C4. Tolerances (ALGO-TOL-1), oracle schemas including PE-P5's delegation_detecting_oracle_fields, and compliance checklists frozen per task, with digests recorded.
C5. Packs built for all ten languages, hashed, read-only, with pack_token_counts.json published including the reference-coverage fields O14 requires.

C6. The 3 (and for UG, 6) worked examples authored for all ten languages, including E6 against the specified failing operation, verified to build and run with the frozen recipes, size-matching residuals published.
C7. The three prompt variations authored and the variation-equivalence check run and preserved.
C9. scripts/classify_version.py, scripts/check_compliance.py, scripts/classify_exhaustion.py and the governing source tokenizer present, with SHA-256 recorded in frozen_input_digests.

C10. A dry run of one non-scored trial per language completed end to end to confirm the harness, the recipes, the oracle, and the preservation layout work; the dry-run directories are kept outside trials/ and are clearly labelled non-scoring. The dry run must include, for all ten languages, a fixture exercising UG-03, UG-04 and UG-09 under the exact frozen recipe.

C10b. For each of the ten languages, the frozen build command is confirmed to succeed against a freshly created trial directory whose build/ directory was created empty by the orchestrator and contains nothing.

C11. Signature-list validation. For each of the ten languages and each of its H1, H2 and runtime-error lists, build and run two fixtures: one that must produce a matching diagnostic and one correct program that must produce none. Preserve the verbatim diagnostic text and the match result at llm-practical/config/signature_validation/<language>.json. A list with no demonstrated positive match, or with a match on its negative fixture, BLOCKS the run until the real diagnostic text is recorded.

C12. Deny-list matcher validation. The argv matcher is run against the fixed 50-legitimate-command corpus per language and the 10-denied-command corpus per language; the false-denial count must be zero for all ten and every denied command must be refused.

C13. Anti-hardcoding validation. Zero hits against the benchmark's own reference implementation in at least three languages, and a hit against the deliberately hard-coded fixture in each of the same three.

C14. LightGrad banned-symbol lists authored for all ten languages, hashed, and validated to both pass (a conforming hand-built implementation) and fail (an implementation that calls a prohibited facility) in at least three languages including Quidra.
C15. client_version captured and recorded in model_and_client_identity.

frozen_input_digests._authority: spec 6.2 ('write an immutable run configuration'); spec 25.4; spec 32.
frozen_input_digests._why: This document declares itself frozen but previously froze none of the inputs it depends on. No task_spec.md, golden file, tolerance file, oracle schema, workload file, pack file or script digest appeared anywhere in it, so an independent analyst holding the document could not tell whether the artefacts a run used were the ones the document describes, and readiness item C2's promise that hashes would be 'recorded' named no location and no value.

frozen_input_digests.invalidation_rule: The run is INVALID if any digest recorded here differs from the digest of the file actually used, at any point. Digests are re-verified at scoring time; a mismatch is recorded in _deviations.json with class 'frozen_input_digest_mismatch' and the affected cells are excluded. A digest is never updated to match an observation.

remediation_changelog._what_this_is: Pre-registration remediation of this frozen run configuration against the adversarial methodology audit recorded at bench/findings/09_llm_run_config_FINDINGS.md. Applied 2026-09-18.
remediation_changelog.no_results_observed: NO SCORE HAS BEEN COMPUTED from this document or from any other document of this methodology, and no scored LLM generation of run 2026-09-17-7677581 has been executed. llm-practical/trials/ contains no trial directory and llm-practical/tasks/ contains no task artefact. Correcting these rules now is legitimate pre-registration, not post-result formula selection, and it is not the change spec 32 and spec 9.1 prohibit. Every rule below is immutable again from the first scored generation onward.
remediation_changelog.correction_direction_policy: Each finding was applied in the direction the auditor specified. No finding was resolved by weakening it, by declaring it out of scope, or by adding a caveat while keeping the biased rule. No compensating bias was introduced in the other direction. Where a correction is expected to LOWER Quidra's score, that is stated plainly below; it is the normal and correct outcome of finding a bias in Quidra's favour.
remediation_changelog.symmetry_test_applied: Every change was checked by substituting Zig and Python for Quidra. No rule added here depends on something Quidra specifically does or lacks; each is stated in terms all ten languages can satisfy or fail. Where a disclosure names Quidra (the reference-coverage asymmetry, the native-mode selection, the overflow-checking configuration), the obligation is written so that whichever language held that position would be the one named.

Added the compliance item 'implemented the differentiation engine in the workload source using general-purpose facilities only', checked against a frozen per-language banned-symbol list. entries.defect: agent_timeout and context_exhausted were classified as infrastructure, retried, and ultimately dropped to N/A rather than scored; a model that burns its whole budget floundering in an unfamiliar language is exhibiting a model/language outcome, and Quidra is by construction the language most likely to trigger it, so its hardest failures were the ones most likely to leave the denominator.
entries.change_applied: Added retry_policy_infrastructure.agent_self_exhaustion_split with a mechanical 300-second stall test over timeline.jsonl and agent_tool_calls.jsonl. Case (a), no completed model turn or tool call in the last 300 s, stays infrastructure and is retried. Case (b), the subagent was still working at the deadline, is subclass agent_budget_exhausted: not retried, classified from whatever exists at generated/ by the ordinary ladder, and SCORED into every metric denominator. Renamed the infrastructure classes to agent_timeout_stalled and context_exhausted_stalled, narrowed the infrastructure_exhausted N/A reason so case (b) can never reach it, added the case to explicitly_not_na, and added obligation O17 requiring the per-language split to be published with the statement that case (b) entered the metrics.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: LOWER. Quidra's budget-exhaustion failures are now scored instead of removed from the denominator.

Quidra's H1/H2 and runtime-error lists are unanchored English substrings with no preserved evidence, so if Quidra 0.2.0's real diagnostics do not match them Quidra records zero hallucinations and scores 100 on a 7 percent metric by instrument failure; meanwhile C++'s list carried 'no matching function for call to' and Go's 'is not a type', which fire on ordinary overload and type errors against symbols that do exist.

entries.defect: The 20,000-token document-order budget is identical in procedure but not in information value: Quidra's reference plausibly fits in full while Python's, C++'s, Rust's, Java's and Swift's are truncated to a document-order prefix of a few percent that is mostly lexical structure and object model. entries.defect: source_token_counting's clause (1) counted a string literal as one token 'regardless of length' with no mention of interpolation, which is exactly the flat one-token-per-hole exemption CORRECTIONS.md D-4 identified as QUIDRA BIAS and removed; none of the three conformance vectors exercised interpolation, so an analyst implementing Source Token Efficiency from this document alone would have reproduced the removed bias.
entries.change_applied: Rewrote clause (1) to the D-4-corrected rule: the literal shell is one token, each interpolation hole pays one token per delimiter actually written (braced or parenthesised forms cost two, a bare sigil costs one), plus the tokens of the embedded expression. Added five conformance vectors covering Quidra print("a={v}") = 7, Python f"x={c}" = 4, Kotlin "x=$c" = 3, Swift "x=\(c)" = 4 and C++ std::format("x={}", c) = 8. On the joint-heaviest metric a silent wrong answer was therefore much more available to other languages than to Quidra, as a build-flag property, and nothing disclosed it.

Added the row to mandatory_published_raw and obligation O16.
