Concentrating Correct@1 on the five-trial primary cell removes precision that was manufactured by averaging; it has no predictable directional effect on any one language, and the change would read the same if Zig or Python were the language under evaluation.

entries.defect: The {{STAGE}} enum named four values while the classifier produces seven; NO_ARTIFACT, SILENT_BUG and COMPLIANCE_FAIL were unmapped, and in the COMPLIANCE_FAIL case the model was told 'Your program did not pass' alongside 'checks passed: T of T' with no field anywhere for the compliance result, leaving a judgement to whoever ran the orchestrator on three metrics worth 17 percent combined.
entries.change_applied: Added exact_repair_prompt_template.stage_mapping_is_total, a total mechanical mapping of all seven classes (NO_ARTIFACT -> NO_SOURCE_FILE_FOUND, COMPILE_FAIL -> PARSE_OR_COMPILE_FAILED / BUILD_TIMED_OUT, RUNTIME_FAIL -> RUNTIME_FAILED / TIMED_OUT, SILENT_BUG and OUTPUT_MISMATCH -> OUTPUT_MISMATCH, COMPLIANCE_FAIL -> COMPLIANCE_FAILED), with per-stage field fills. Added a '--- COMPLIANCE RESULT ---' block to the repair prompt carrying 'compliance items satisfied: P of K' and the verbatim failing item ids with no interpretation, present byte-identically for all ten languages and filled with its N/A literal when there is nothing to report.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL. The template change is language-independent and removes orchestrator discretion rather than moving any language.

entries.defect: The anti-hardcoding check, the only mechanism that can force FAIL on an otherwise passing program, turned on the undefined phrase 'not derivable as a task-specified constant' and stated two incompatible procedures at once (automatic FAIL, and human review of the hit list), with the human-review branch injecting human judgement into a pipeline declared mechanical.
entries.change_applied: Defined the exemption set mechanically and exhaustively: a numeric literal is exempt iff its normalised decimal text appears verbatim in that task's task_spec.md, or it is one of 0, 1, 2, -1, 0.5, or one of the LCG constants 48271 and 2147483647. Specified exactly what is searched (non-exempt numeric literals against golden float and integer fields, string literals against golden output lines). Stated ONE procedure: a hit sets the compliance item to fail and the classification to COMPLIANCE_FAIL, mechanically, with no human review; the hit list is preserved so a third party can audit the rule, and a false positive is reported in _deviations.json and not overturned within the run. Added readiness item C13 requiring zero hits against the benchmark's own reference in three languages and a hit against a deliberately hard-coded fixture in each.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL. Applies identically to all ten and removes a discretionary override.

entries.defect: Three PE-P1 compliance items had no stated detection method and one, 'no file written outside build/', contradicted tool_permissions, which grants the agent Write and Edit on <trial>/scratch/ - an agent using the directory it was given would have failed part of a 7 percent metric.
entries.change_applied: Added common_task_contract.compliance_predicates, rewriting every affected item as an observable predicate on the PROGRAM under the frozen run command: path-set snapshot around the run for no-file-written-outside-build (with the agent's authoring-time writes, including scratch/, explicitly out of scope); /dev/null versus a 1 MiB fixed byte stream for no-stdin-read; three appended ignored arguments for no-arguments-consulted; three runs for determinism; regex on printed bytes for decimal places; and a named oracle_schema field (LCG_PROBE_U5, the 5th unit float at the task's seed, printed to 12 decimals) replacing the unimplementable LCG-seed item. Rewrote PE-P1's checklist accordingly and gave PE-P5/PE-P6 a checklist for the first time.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL. Language-independent predicates; no language gains or loses relative to another.

entries.defect: Two family-C metrics made their workload set depend on the language: Generated Code Performance stated two different aggregations in one sentence, and Source Token Efficiency averaged only over 'the tasks where it does have' a passing version, so a language was scored only on the tasks it succeeded at and failing the task on which it would have been most verbose RAISED its score.
entries.change_applied: Fixed the applicable workload set before the run and made it language-independent: {PE-P1-svm-specA} for Generated Code Performance, Memory Efficiency and Compile Performance, with score 0 where there is no passing version; {PE-P1..PE-P6} for Source Token Efficiency, with a per-task score of 0 (not an omission) for any of the six with no passing version. Deleted the 'mean over the tasks where it does have one' clause and added the case to na_policy.explicitly_not_na.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: LOWER. Quidra, as the language likeliest to have no passing version on some of the six tasks, loses the conditioning-on-success relief; the same is true of any language in that position.

entries.defect: The frozen TypeScript build command pinned no target, so tsc ran at its default, where BigInt literals are rejected; UG-03 and UG-04 require exact values outside binary64 and need BigInt, so TypeScript would have failed two of twelve UG cases for a harness-configuration reason that spec 10.4(b) says the harness must absorb. Java and Kotlin carried the same class of unverified risk if the model declared a package.
entries.change_applied: Pinned the TypeScript recipe to 'tsc --target es2022 --module commonjs --outDir build generated/main.ts' and recorded it under a new per_language_placeholder_substitutions.harness_configuration_pins block as a C-4 harness responsibility; added the Java and Kotlin no-package / top-level entry-point convention to the build_run_recipe.txt slot that already exists for all ten; extended readiness item C10 to require the dry run to exercise UG-03, UG-04 and UG-09 under the exact frozen recipe for all ten languages.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: LOWER, relatively. TypeScript stops losing two UG cases to a flag, so Quidra's relative position on a 6 percent metric falls.

entries.defect: (a) UG-09 required integer division by zero to be 'detected and reported' with the program continuing, which is impossible via the trap in C++, Swift and Zig and non-idiomatic in Rust, while a language with a catchable checked division passes naturally; the document nevertheless claimed UG-09 as a case where Quidra's error model makes things HARDER, which is the reverse of the truth. (b) PE-P2/P4/P6 did not say whether the source shown is the upstream repository or the reduced implementation that produced the golden, which decides whether a faithful port passes at all.
entries.change_applied: (a) Added the frozen sentence accepting EITHER the attempt-and-handle form OR the guard form, scoring only the printed ERROR:DIVZERO line, the continuation and exit status 0, with the reason stated in terms of all ten languages' fault models; removed UG-09 from the fairness_statement's list of cases claimed to be harder for Quidra and replaced the claim with the accurate one, which is that the case as written FAVOURED Quidra. (b) Added reference_source_identity to PE-P2, PE-P4 and PE-P6 stating that the shown source is byte-identical to the frozen reduced reference that generated the golden, with its SHA-256 in frozen_input_digests and the same bytes for all ten.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: LOWER. A UG case that quietly favoured Quidra's error model now asks all ten the same question, and a false claim of Quidra hardship has been withdrawn.

entries.defect: managed_runtime_handling promised that cold-start and steady-state numbers are 'never mixed' but never said which enters the score, and the stated protocol (fresh process per run) produces no steady-state number at all, making the promise unfalsifiable.
entries.change_applied: Stated explicitly that each of the 3 warm-up and 7 measured runs is a fresh process, that the scored raw value therefore includes runtime startup and JIT warm-up for Java, Kotlin, TypeScript/node and Python and process start for the compiled languages, and that this is the scored figure for all ten. Named the in-process steady-state protocol (one process, workload body executed 10 times, median of the last 7), required it for all ten rather than only the managed runtimes, and marked it non-scoring.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL. Naming which figure is scored does not move any language; running the diagnostic for all ten keeps it from being a managed-runtime accommodation.

entries.defect: Spec 11 asks for a rule COMBINING Quidra's native and interpreter evidence; the document instead SELECTED native, the faster mode, for Generated Code Performance and Memory Efficiency, and never made the effect of that selection visible.
entries.change_applied: Relabelled the rule 'SELECTION, NOT COMBINATION' in both places it appears, stated that native is the most Quidra-favourable available selection for these two metrics, and added obligation O15 requiring Quidra's whole LLM Practical Effectiveness Score to be republished recomputed with interpreter-mode values substituted, beside the primary score, with the same obligation stated for any language the run measures in more than one execution mode.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: LOWER in interpretation. The score itself is unchanged, but the reader now sees what the Quidra-favourable mode selection is worth.

entries.defect: api_version_string was null on the ground that the provider API version is not exposed, but spec 6.2 asks for 'API OR client version' and the client version is obtainable, so a mandatory 6.2 field was left unfilled when a value existed.
entries.change_applied: Added model_and_client_identity.client_version with a capture rule (the Claude Code CLI / Agent SDK version string, captured once before the first scored trial, repeated per trial in manifest.json as client_version_reported, with a client_version_mismatch deviation class), kept api_version_string null with its reason narrowed to the provider API, and added readiness item C15.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL.

entries.defect: fairness_declaration.nothing_derived_from_quidra asserted that no metric, tolerance or task in the document was derived from Quidra's feature set, while the run's own C-1 records that the Park-Miller generator was selected under a constraint that includes Quidra's overflow-checked integers - the first contradiction an auditor comparing the two files would find.
entries.change_applied: Amended the clause to state the single disclosed exception explicitly, naming C-1, its neutrality argument and its verification that the generator needs no workaround and grants no shortcut in any of the ten. Also extended no_capability_removed to point at the new PE-P5/P6 prohibited_facilities, which removes a Quidra advantage rather than a capability.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL on the number; it replaces an over-broad neutrality claim with an accurate one.

entries.defect: tool_permissions granted Write and Edit on <trial>/scratch/ but the preservation layout had no scratch/ entry, so the agent's working files were destroyed, weakening the spec 23 reconstruction guarantee; and the system prompt never told the model the directory existed, so the affordance was unusable.
entries.change_applied: Added <trial>/scratch/ to the preserved directory tree with file semantics saying it is preserved read-only and never scored, and added to system-prompt rule 1: 'You may write working files under {{WORKDIR}}/scratch/; nothing there is scored, and it is preserved for audit.' The system-prompt change is made before the first scored generation, as the finding requires, and is recorded here and in _deviations.json as a pre_freeze_amendment.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL. The affordance becomes real and identical for all ten.

entries.defect: PromptRobustness (the minimum of three 5-trial rates, which is biased low and coarser than a single 5-trial rate) and Correct@N (four binary cells, five attainable values) both have resolution worse than the published floor, and obligation O2 covered neither because both are backed by five-trial cells.
entries.change_applied: Added PromptRobustness, Correct@N and Correct@1_scored entries to resolution_floor with their attainable value sets and the downward-bias note, and extended O2 to cover every row whose scored value can take fewer than ten distinct values, stating the attainable set.
entries.direction_of_effect_on_quidra_expected_s: NEUTRAL.

self_review_beyond_the_brief: Checked for a capability quietly omitted because Quidra cannot do it: none found beyond finding 1, which was the inverse case (a capability Quidra alone HAS, left available). The UG case set retains UG-03, UG-04 and UG-08, which Quidra's overflow-checked integers make harder, and C-7 records that Quidra 0.2.0 has no bitwise operators at all without any workload being weakened for it.

Checked for double counting: Repair Success Rate (7 percent) and Repair Efficiency (5 percent) both respond to the same repair outcome, and a trial still failing after repair_03 is penalised in both. The eighteen metrics and their weights are copied unaltered from spec 9.1 and may not be changed here; the overlap is the spec's design, it is symmetric across all ten languages, and it is recorded rather than adjusted. No new double count was introduced by this remediation.

Checked the N/A policy after the changes: the four permitted reason codes are harness_does_not_expose_token_usage (all ten or none), language_has_no_separate_build_step_in_its_frozen_recipe (a genuinely absent quantity, with the cost still visible inside Generated Code Performance), no_failing_initial_generation, and infrastructure_exhausted (now reachable only through a genuine provider or transport stall). None of them lets a missing capability escape the low score spec 26 requires, and explicitly_not_na was extended with three new cases.

Checked aggregation shapes: Correct@1 no longer averages a mandated five-trial cell into nine low-resolution ones (finding 12), and no family-C metric averages over a language-dependent task set (finding 16). Silent Bug Resistance and Syntax Hallucination Resistance remain pooled, which is measurement rather than averaging.

Checked neutral-in-one-section / exempt-in-another: the four instances found are findings 1 (rule 2 versus C-6), 9 (identical procedure presented as identical information), 15 (no-file-written versus the granted scratch/ permission) and 22 (nothing_derived_from_quidra versus C-1). All four are corrected on this side.

Finding 17 and finding 8.

C-4 must record the pinned TypeScript target/module flags and the Java/Kotlin no-package entry-point convention as harness responsibilities, alongside the existing --outFile and Zig Io-instance notes. Finding 17.

ALGO-TOL-1's applies_to should name the LLM-track task ids PE-P1 through PE-P6 alongside WL-SVM, WL-GMM and WL-LG, so the adoption recorded here is visible from the tolerance file itself. No numeric value changes. Finding 6.

Section 1.9's 'standard library only' must carry the C-6 prohibition inline for all ten languages, and the frozen per-language banned-symbol list (llm-practical/config/lightgrad_banned_symbols.json) must be derived from and kept identical to 07's list. The exact-match integer stability pre-flight of finding 6 applies to WL-SVM and WL-GMM on 07's side as well. Findings 1 and 6.

Section 4.4(a) must remain as corrected by CORRECTIONS.md D-4 (one token per delimiter actually written), and the tokenizer must remain the single implementation used by both the Semantic Compression track and Source Token Efficiency, with its SHA-256 recorded in this document's frozen_input_digests. Finding 10.

Record the 2026-09-18 pre-freeze amendments to this document's system prompt and repair prompt template (findings 1, 13 and 23) as a defect-and-fix entry, since spec 10.4 requires defects found during a run to be recorded rather than silently corrected. Also record the withdrawal of the PE-P1 and PE-P3 tolerances in favour of ALGO-TOL-1. Findings 1, 6, 13, 23.
